knowledge_statements.statement_title: Mixed-strategy minimax theorem for finite matrix games
knowledge_statements.scope_note: States the equality between the minimizing player's worst-case payoff and the maximizing player's guaranteed payoff, together with its primal-dual LP representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P\in\mathbb R^{n\times m}\), \(\Delta_n=\{u\in\mathbb R^n:u\succeq0,\ \mathbf1^Tu=1\}\), and \(\Delta_m=\{v\in\mathbb R^m:v\succeq0,\ \mathbf1^Tv=1\}\). For independently selected mixed strategies, the expected payment from player 1 to player 2 is \(u^TPv\). Define \[p_1^\star=\min_{u\in\Delta_n}\max_{v\in\Delta_m}u^TPv=\min_{u\in\Delta_n}\max_{1\le j\le m}(P^Tu)_j\] and \[p_2^\star=\max_{v\in\Delta_m}\min_{u\in\Delta_n}u^TPv=\max_{v\in\Delta_m}\min_{1\le i\le n}(Pv)_i.\] Then \[p_1^\star=p_2^\star.\] The epigraph LP for \(p_1^\star\) and the hypograph LP for \(p_2^\star\) are a feasible primal-dual LP pair, so their optimal values coincide.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: In every finite two-player zero-sum matrix game, the smallest worst-case expected payment achievable by the minimizing player equals the largest expected payment guaranteed by the maximizing player. The two mixed-strategy optimization problems have feasible primal-dual linear-programming formulations with the same value.
assumptions_latex: u\in\Delta_n,\ v\in\Delta_m\text{ are independently selected mixed strategies}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \min_{u\in\Delta_n}\max_{v\in\Delta_m}u^TPv=\max_{v\in\Delta_m}\min_{u\in\Delta_n}u^TPv

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Polynomial-Size Conversion of a General LP to Karmarkar Form
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reduction preserving polynomial encoding length and supplying the uniform feasible start and, optionally, a zero-optimum formulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\min\{\mathbf c\mathbf x:\mathbf A\mathbf x=\mathbf b,\ \mathbf x\geq0\}\) have integer data, \(\mathbf A\in\mathbb Z^{m\times n}\) with \(\operatorname{rank}(\mathbf A)=m\), and input length \(L\). Choose an integer bound \(Q\) for \(\sum_jx_j\) (with \(Q=2^L\) available in the worst case), add a slack variable, introduce a homogenizing variable, and scale by \(Q+1\). Adding an artificial variable \(y_{n+3}\) with coefficients whose homogeneous-constraint columns sum to zero gives the Karmarkar-form problem \[\min\ \mathbf c\mathbf y+My_{n+3}\] subject to \[\mathbf A\mathbf y-\mathbf b y_{n+2}-(\mathbf A\mathbf1^T-\mathbf b)y_{n+3}=0,\] \[\mathbf1\mathbf y+y_{n+1}-Qy_{n+2}-(n+1-Q)y_{n+3}=0,\qquad \mathbf1\mathbf y+y_{n+1}+y_{n+2}+y_{n+3}=1,\] \[y_j\geq0\quad(j=1,\ldots,n+3).\] Its uniform point \((1/(n+3),\ldots,1/(n+3))^T\) is feasible. A choice \(|M|=2^{O(L)}\) ensures \(y_{n+3}=0\) at optimality whenever the pre-artificial problem is feasible, and the transformed input length remains \(O(L)\). To enforce zero optimal value, put the primal-dual optimality system \(\mathbf A\mathbf x=\mathbf b,\ \mathbf x\geq0,\ \mathbf w\mathbf A\leq\mathbf c,\ \mathbf c\mathbf x=\mathbf w\mathbf b\) into nonnegative equality form and apply the same construction with objective \(\min y_{n+3}\). If the original LP has an optimum, the transformed optimum is zero and yields primal and dual optimal solutions. Otherwise its optimum is positive; failure to reduce it below \(2^{-L'}\) within \(10n'L'\) iterations identifies the infeasible-or-unbounded alternative, which is resolved by separate primal- and dual-feasibility tests.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A full-row-rank equality-form LP with integer data can be bounded, homogenized, scaled to a simplex equality, and augmented by an artificial variable so that the uniform point is feasible. The transformation has encoding length O(L), and a polynomially bounded big-M coefficient forces the artificial variable to zero whenever the underlying formulation is feasible. Applying the construction to the primal-dual optimality system produces a zero-optimum Karmarkar problem exactly when the original LP has an optimum and recovers both optimal solutions; a positive artificial optimum indicates infeasibility or unboundedness, distinguishable through primal and dual feasibility tests.
assumptions_latex: \mathbf b,\mathbf c\text{ are integer data and the original input length is }L
Q\in\mathbb Z\text{ bounds }\sum_{j=1}^n x_j\text{ over the relevant feasible or optimal solutions}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{The constructed problem is in normalized Karmarkar form, has input length }O(L),\text{ and has a uniform feasible point; the primal-dual variant has optimum }0\iff\text{the original LP has an optimum.}

children.top_down_role: Canonical pairings organized around one-sided linear constraints.

knowledge_statements.title: Inequality-Form Pairs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical maximization–minimization pair with nonnegative variables and one-sided inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb{R}^m\), and \(c\in\mathbb{R}^n\), the primal inequality-form program and its dual are
\[ (P)\quad \max\{c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax\le b,\ x\ge0\}, \qquad (D)\quad \min\{b^{\mathsf T}y:A^{\mathsf T}y\ge c,\ y\ge0\}. \]
Every primal-feasible \(x\) and dual-feasible \(y\) satisfy \(c^{\mathsf T}x\le b^{\mathsf T}y\). If both programs have optimal solutions and either has a finite optimal value, their optimal values coincide.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A maximization LP with upper inequalities and nonnegative variables pairs with a minimization LP having transposed lower inequalities and nonnegative variables.
assumptions_latex: The displayed strong-duality conclusion assumes finite attained optima.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(c^{\mathsf T}x\le b^{\mathsf T}y\) for feasible pairs, and \(\max(P)=\min(D)\) when finite optima are attained.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Proposed gap and complementarity statement is mathematically sound but is primarily owned by the dedicated complementarity topics.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For primal-feasible \(x\ge0\) with \(Ax\le b\) and dual-feasible \(y\ge0\) with \(A^\top y\ge c\), \[b^\top y-c^\top x=y^\top(b-Ax)+x^\top(A^\top y-c)\ge0.\] Consequently, the gap is zero exactly when all associated complementarity products vanish.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The duality gap decomposes into primal-slack and dual-slack complementarity products.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: b^\top y-c^\top x=y^\top(b-Ax)+x^\top(A^\top y-c)\ge0

knowledge_statements.title: Equality-Constraint Side
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Effect of a primal equality constraint on the corresponding dual variable.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider
\[ (P)\quad \max\{c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax=b,\ x\ge0\}. \]
Its dual-side representation is
\[ (D)\quad \min\{b^{\mathsf T}y:A^{\mathsf T}y\ge c,\ y\in\mathbb{R}^m\}, \]
where \(y\) is unrestricted in sign. Equivalently, each equality row may be replaced by two opposite inequalities; the difference of their nonnegative multipliers yields the free component of \(y\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each equality constraint in the primal corresponds to a sign-unrestricted dual variable.
assumptions_latex: The primal is written as a maximization problem with \(x\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The multiplier of \(Ax=b\) satisfies \(y\in\mathbb{R}^m\) with no sign restriction.

notation.meaning: multiplier associated with the equality constraints

knowledge_statements.title: Nonnegative-Variable Side
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Effect of a nonnegative primal variable on the corresponding dual constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For the equality-form primal
\[ (P)\quad \max\{c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax=b,\ x\ge0\}, \]
the dual is
\[ (D)\quad \min\{b^{\mathsf T}y:A^{\mathsf T}y\ge c,\ y\in\mathbb{R}^m\}. \]
Thus each restriction \(x_j\ge0\) corresponds to the dual inequality \(a_j^{\mathsf T}y\ge c_j\), where \(a_j\) is column \(j\) of \(A\). The inequality ensures that increasing the nonnegative coordinate \(x_j\) cannot violate weak duality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each nonnegative primal variable induces a dual constraint whose left side dominates its objective coefficient.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For every \(j\), \(x_j\ge0\) corresponds to \(a_j^{\mathsf T}y\ge c_j\).

notation.meaning: column j of the primal constraint matrix

knowledge_statements.title: Equality–Nonnegativity Correspondence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Row–multiplier and column–constraint correspondence for equality-form linear programs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Under the maximization convention, the pair
\[ \max\{c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax=b,\ x\ge0\},\qquad \min\{b^{\mathsf T}y:A^{\mathsf T}y\ge c,\ y\text{ free}\} \]
exhibits two reciprocal rules: a primal equality row produces a free dual variable, while a nonnegative primal variable produces a dual inequality of sense \(\ge\). Conversely, the free dual variable corresponds to the primal equality, and the dual inequality corresponds to the nonnegative primal variable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Primal equalities correspond to free dual variables, while nonnegative primal variables correspond to dual inequalities.
assumptions_latex: The primal uses the maximization convention.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Ax=b\leftrightarrow y\text{ free}\) and \(x\ge0\leftrightarrow A^{\mathsf T}y\ge c\).

knowledge_statements.title: Symmetric Primal-Dual Pairs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Parallel inequality-form presentation in which both programs have nonnegative variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb{R}^m\), and \(c\in\mathbb{R}^n\), a symmetric primal-dual pair is
\[ (P)\quad \min\{c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax\ge b,\ x\ge0\},\qquad (D)\quad \max\{b^{\mathsf T}y:A^{\mathsf T}y\le c,\ y\ge0\}. \]
The programs exchange variables with constraints and replace \(A\) by \(A^{\mathsf T}\). Feasible pairs satisfy \(b^{\mathsf T}y\le c^{\mathsf T}x\), and finite attained optima have equal objective values.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The symmetric pair exchanges variables and constraints, transposes the matrix, and reverses objective orientation and inequality sense.
assumptions_latex: Equality of optimal values assumes finite attained optima.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(b^{\mathsf T}y\le c^{\mathsf T}x\) for feasible pairs, with equality of finite attained optimal values.

notation.meaning: transpose of the primal constraint matrix

knowledge_statements.title: Constraint-Variable Correspondence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Structural row–variable and column–constraint exchange under LP dualization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a primal LP have matrix \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\). Dualization assigns one dual variable \(y_i\) to each primal constraint row \(i\), and one dual constraint to each primal variable \(x_j\). Consequently the dual matrix is \(A^{\mathsf T}\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times m}\): primal row coefficients become dual-variable coefficients, and primal column coefficients become dual-constraint coefficients. Constraint senses determine dual-variable signs, while primal-variable signs determine dual-constraint senses.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each primal constraint creates a dual variable, and each primal variable creates a dual constraint; matrix transposition records this exchange.
assumptions_latex: The primal has \(m\) scalar constraints, \(n\) scalar variables, and matrix \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The dual has \(m\) variables, \(n\) constraints, and coefficient matrix \(A^{\mathsf T}\).

notation.meaning: dual variable corresponding to primal row i
primal variable corresponding to dual constraint j

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Dual of a General-Form Minimization LP
knowledge_statements.scope_note: General primal–dual construction for mixed constraint senses and variable-sign domains. Under the source convention, a maximization primal is converted to an equivalent minimization problem before dualization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For the primal problem
\[
\min_x c^\top x
\]
subject to
\[
a_i^\top x\ge b_i\ (i\in M_1),\quad a_i^\top x\le b_i\ (i\in M_2),\quad a_i^\top x=b_i\ (i\in M_3),
\]
and
\[
x_j\ge0\ (j\in N_1),\quad x_j\le0\ (j\in N_2),\quad x_j\text{ free}\ (j\in N_3),
\]
the dual is
\[
\max_p p^\top b
\]
subject to
\[
p_i\ge0\ (i\in M_1),\quad p_i\le0\ (i\in M_2),\quad p_i\text{ free}\ (i\in M_3),
\]
and
\[
p^\top A_j\le c_j\ (j\in N_1),\quad p^\top A_j\ge c_j\ (j\in N_2),\quad p^\top A_j=c_j\ (j\in N_3).
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each primal constraint produces a dual variable: a greater-than constraint gives a nonnegative variable, a less-than constraint gives a nonpositive variable, and an equality gives a free variable. Each primal variable produces a dual constraint: a nonnegative variable gives a less-than constraint, a nonpositive variable gives a greater-than constraint, and a free variable gives an equality. The dual maximizes p-transpose b.
assumptions_latex: A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\text{ has rows }a_i^\top\text{ and columns }A_j.
(M_1,M_2,M_3)\text{ partitions the primal constraint indices according to their senses}.
(N_1,N_2,N_3)\text{ partitions the primal variable indices according to their sign domains}.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: D(P)=\max_p\left\{p^\top b:\ p_i\ge0\ (i\in M_1),\ p_i\le0\ (i\in M_2),\ p_i\text{ free}\ (i\in M_3),\ p^\top A_j\le c_j\ (j\in N_1),\ p^\top A_j\ge c_j\ (j\in N_2),\ p^\top A_j=c_j\ (j\in N_3)\right\}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Dualization rules for a mixed-form minimization LP
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Direct dual construction for mixed primal constraint senses and variable sign restrictions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider a minimization LP with objective $c^\top x$. A primal row $a_i^\top x\ge b_i$, $a_i^\top x\le b_i$, or $a_i^\top x=b_i$ produces a dual variable satisfying respectively $w_i\ge0$, $w_i\le0$, or $w_i$ unrestricted. A primal variable satisfying $x_j\ge0$, $x_j\le0$, or $x_j$ unrestricted produces respectively the dual constraint $(A^\top w)_j\le c_j$, $(A^\top w)_j\ge c_j$, or $(A^\top w)_j=c_j$. The dual objective is $\max b^\top w$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a mixed-form minimization LP, greater-than, less-than, and equality rows correspond respectively to nonnegative, nonpositive, and unrestricted dual variables. Nonnegative, nonpositive, and unrestricted primal variables correspond respectively to less-than, greater-than, and equality dual constraints. The dual maximizes b transpose w.
assumptions_latex: \mathrm{(P)}\text{ is a real finite-dimensional minimization LP with compatible mixed row senses and variable sign restrictions}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathrm{(D)}:\ \max b^\top w,\quad \begin{cases}w_i\ge0&\text{if row }i\text{ is }\ge,\\w_i\le0&\text{if row }i\text{ is }\le,\\w_i\text{ free}&\text{if row }i\text{ is }=,\end{cases}\quad \begin{cases}(A^\top w)_j\le c_j&\text{if }x_j\ge0,\\(A^\top w)_j\ge c_j&\text{if }x_j\le0,\\(A^\top w)_j=c_j&\text{if }x_j\text{ is free}.\end{cases}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Partial Lagrangian dual of a linearly constrained problem over a polyhedron
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dualizes the block Ax≥b while retaining the polyhedral restriction x∈P in the inner problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(P=\{x\mid Dx\ge d\}\) and consider \(\min\{c^{\mathsf T}x\mid Ax\ge b,\ x\in P\}\). Associate a multiplier \(p\) only with \(Ax\ge b\). Define
\[
g(p)=\min_{x\in P}\bigl[c^{\mathsf T}x+p^{\mathsf T}(b-Ax)\bigr].
\]
The corresponding dual problem is
\[
\max_{p\ge0}g(p).
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a linear program minimizing cᵀx subject to Ax≥b and x in the polyhedron P={x: Dx≥d}, assign nonnegative multipliers only to Ax≥b. The dual function minimizes cᵀx+pᵀ(b−Ax) over x in P, and the dual problem maximizes this function over p≥0.
assumptions_latex: p\text{ is associated only with }Ax\ge b
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: g(p)=\min_{x\in P}\left[c^{\mathsf T}x+p^{\mathsf T}(b-Ax)\right],\qquad \max_{p\ge0}g(p)

children.top_down_role: Dualization regimes involving equality, upper-bound, and lower-bound constraint senses.

knowledge_statements.title: Mixed Constraint-Sense Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dual-variable sign restrictions induced by mixed primal constraint senses.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Partition the rows of a maximization LP into \(I_{\le}\), \(I_{=}\), and \(I_{\ge}\), according as the primal constraint is \(a_i^{\mathsf T}x\le b_i\), \(a_i^{\mathsf T}x=b_i\), or \(a_i^{\mathsf T}x\ge b_i\). The associated dual multiplier satisfies
\[ y_i\ge0\quad(i\in I_{\le}),\qquad y_i\in\mathbb{R}\quad(i\in I_=),\qquad y_i\le0\quad(i\in I_{\ge}). \]
These componentwise rules allow all three constraint senses to coexist in one primal program.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: In a maximization LP, upper, equality, and lower constraints generate nonnegative, free, and nonpositive dual variables, respectively.
assumptions_latex: Each primal row has sense \(\le\), \(=\), or \(\ge\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(i\in I_{\le}\Rightarrow y_i\ge0\), \(i\in I_=\Rightarrow y_i\text{ free}\), and \(i\in I_{\ge}\Rightarrow y_i\le0\).

notation.meaning: row-index sets classified by primal constraint sense

children.title: Mixed Variable-Sign Regimes
children.top_down_role: Dualization regimes involving nonnegative, nonpositive, and free variables.

knowledge_statements.title: Mixed Variable-Sign Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dual-constraint senses induced by mixed primal variable sign restrictions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a maximization LP, partition variable indices into \(J_+\), \(J_-\), and \(J_0\), according as \(x_j\ge0\), \(x_j\le0\), or \(x_j\in\mathbb{R}\). If \(a_j\) is column \(j\) of the primal matrix, the corresponding dual constraints are
\[ a_j^{\mathsf T}y\ge c_j\quad(j\in J_+),\qquad a_j^{\mathsf T}y\le c_j\quad(j\in J_-),\qquad a_j^{\mathsf T}y=c_j\quad(j\in J_0). \]
Thus different sign regimes may be dualized componentwise.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nonnegative, nonpositive, and free primal variables induce lower, upper, and equality dual constraints, respectively.
assumptions_latex: Every primal variable is nonnegative, nonpositive, or free.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_j\ge0\Rightarrow a_j^{\mathsf T}y\ge c_j\), \(x_j\le0\Rightarrow a_j^{\mathsf T}y\le c_j\), and \(x_j\text{ free}\Rightarrow a_j^{\mathsf T}y=c_j\).

knowledge_statements.title: Sense–Sign Dual Correspondence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Complete sense–sign lookup rule under the primal-maximization convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a primal maximization LP, dualization obeys the componentwise correspondences
\[ \text{primal row }\le,=,\ge\quad\longleftrightarrow\quad\text{dual variable }\ge0,\text{ free},\le0, \]
\[ \text{primal variable }\ge0,\le0,\text{ free}\quad\longleftrightarrow\quad\text{dual constraint }\ge,\le,=. \]
Applying the same rule to the dual, with maximization and minimization roles exchanged, recovers the primal after identifying \(A^{\mathsf{TT}}=A\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Constraint senses determine dual-variable signs, and variable signs determine dual-constraint senses; the rules are reciprocal.

All variables and constraints are finite-dimensional and real.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Row sense and dual-variable sign, and variable sign and dual-row sense, are reciprocal correspondences.

children.title: Objective-Orientation Conventions
children.top_down_role: Equivalent minimization and maximization conventions for presenting primal-dual pairs.

knowledge_statements.title: Objective-Orientation Conventions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalence between maximization–minimization and sign-reversed minimization–maximization presentations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
If \((P)\) maximizes \(c^{\mathsf T}x\) over a feasible set \(X\) and \((D)\) minimizes \(b^{\mathsf T}y\) over a feasible set \(Y\), then the sign-reversed programs
\[ (P')\quad\min_{x\in X}(-c^{\mathsf T}x),\qquad (D')\quad\max_{y\in Y}(-b^{\mathsf T}y) \]
have the same feasible and optimal solution sets as \((P)\) and \((D)\), respectively. Their optimal values are negated, so \(\max(P)=\min(D)\) is equivalent to \(\min(P')=\max(D')\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Negating both objectives converts a max–min primal-dual presentation into an equivalent min–max presentation with negated values.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) and \(Y\) are the unchanged primal and dual feasible sets.
The compared optimal values exist in the extended-real sense.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{val}(P')=-\operatorname{val}(P)\) and \(\operatorname{val}(D')=-\operatorname{val}(D)\).

children.title: Bounded-Variable Duality
children.top_down_role: Dual representations that retain explicit variable bounds or convert them into ordinary constraints.

knowledge_statements.title: Bounded-Variable Duality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dualization retaining finite lower and upper bounds as explicit multiplier terms.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For finite vectors \(l,u\in\mathbb{R}^n\) with \(l\le u\), consider
\[ (P)\quad\max\{c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax\le b,\ l\le x\le u\}. \]
Treating \(x\) as free and assigning nonnegative multipliers \(y\), \(\alpha\), and \(\beta\) to \(Ax\le b\), \(x\le u\), and \(-x\le-l\), respectively, gives
\[ (D)\quad\min\{b^{\mathsf T}y+u^{\mathsf T}\alpha-l^{\mathsf T}\beta:A^{\mathsf T}y+\alpha-\beta=c,\ y,\alpha,\beta\ge0\}. \]
This is the ordinary-constraint representation of bounded-variable duality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Explicit lower and upper bounds produce nonnegative dual multipliers and corresponding lower- and upper-bound terms in the dual objective.
assumptions_latex: \(l\le u\) componentwise and both bounds are finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The dual equality is \(A^{\mathsf T}y+\alpha-\beta=c\), with objective \(b^{\mathsf T}y+u^{\mathsf T}\alpha-l^{\mathsf T}\beta\).

source_refs.locator: 5.2 The Simplex Method for Bounded Variables p. 220
6.2 Primal-Dual Relationships p. 264

source_witnesses.locator: 5.2 The Simplex Method for Bounded Variables p. 220
6.2 Primal-Dual Relationships p. 264

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bound-multiplier dualization when only selected variable bounds are finite.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(L=\{j:l_j> -\infty\}\) and \(U=\{j:u_j<+\infty\}\). For \(P=\max\{c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax\le b,\ l\le x\le u\}\), introduce \(\beta_j\ge0\) only for \(j\in L\) and \(\alpha_j\ge0\) only for \(j\in U\), extending absent components by zero. The dual is
\[\min\left\{b^{\mathsf T}y+\sum_{j\in U}u_j\alpha_j-\sum_{j\in L}l_j\beta_j:A^{\mathsf T}y+\alpha-\beta=c,\ y,\alpha_U,\beta_L\ge0\right\}.\]
Thus a free variable has neither bound multiplier, a one-sided variable has one, and a two-sided finite variable has both.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Only finite lower or upper bounds generate bound multipliers; free, one-sided, and two-sided variables are obtained by omitting the multipliers for absent bounds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A finite upper bound contributes \(u_j\alpha_j\), a finite lower bound contributes \(-l_j\beta_j\), and an absent bound contributes no multiplier or objective term.

notation.meaning: indices having finite lower and upper bounds, respectively
upper- and lower-bound multipliers, extended by zero where absent

knowledge_statements.title: Partial and Infinite Bound Regimes

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalent elimination of explicit lower- and upper-bound multipliers when all bounds are finite.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(P=\max\{c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax\le b,\ l\le x\le u\}\) with finite \(l\le u\), let \(B=[l,u]\) and \(r(y)=c-A^{\mathsf T}y\). Eliminating the bound multipliers gives
\[\inf_{y\ge0}\{b^{\mathsf T}y+\sigma_B(r(y))\},\qquad \sigma_B(r)=\sum_{j=1}^n\begin{cases}u_jr_j,&r_j\ge0,\\l_jr_j,&r_j\le0.\end{cases}\]
Equivalently, \(\sigma_B(r)=\min\{u^{\mathsf T}\alpha-l^{\mathsf T}\beta:\alpha-\beta=r,\ \alpha,\beta\ge0\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With finite two-sided bounds, bound multipliers can be eliminated into the support function of the bound box.
assumptions_latex: \(l\le u\) componentwise and all endpoints are finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{val}(D)=\inf_{y\ge0}\{b^{\mathsf T}y+\sigma_{[l,u]}(c-A^{\mathsf T}y)\}\).

notation.meaning: support function of the bound box
objective residual after pricing structural rows

children.title: Dual Variables
children.top_down_role: Dual-coordinate objects arising from a primal-dual LP representation.

knowledge_statements.title: Dual Variables
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dual variables as scalar multipliers indexed by primal constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a primal linear program with scalar constraint rows indexed by \(i=1,\ldots,m\), a dual variable \(y_i\) is the scalar multiplier assigned to primal row \(i\) in the dual construction. The vector \(y=(y_1,\ldots,y_m)\) enters the dual objective through \(b^{\mathsf T}y\) and the dual constraints through \(A^{\mathsf T}y\). Its admissible sign is fixed by the sense of the associated primal constraint and the chosen objective-orientation convention; an equality row produces a free multiplier.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A dual variable is the multiplier associated with one primal constraint and becomes a coordinate of the dual decision vector.
assumptions_latex: The primal has finitely many scalar linear constraints with matrix \(A\) and right-hand side \(b\).
A fixed primal objective-orientation convention is used.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Primal row \(i\) is represented by dual coordinate \(y_i\), and all multipliers form \(y\in\mathbb{R}^m\) subject to sense-dependent signs.

notation.meaning: dual variable associated with primal constraint i

children.title: Constraint Multipliers

knowledge_statements.title: Constraint Multipliers
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Multipliers for inequality constraints in a canonical maximization LP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the primal program \\(\max\{c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax\le b,\ x\ge0\}\\), a constraint-multiplier vector is \\(y\in\mathbb R_+^m\\). Its Lagrangian is \\(L(x,y)=c^{\mathsf T}x+y^{\mathsf T}(b-Ax)\\). The supremum of \\(L(x,y)\\) over \\(x\ge0\\) is finite precisely when \\(A^{\mathsf T}y\ge c\\), in which case it equals \\(b^{\mathsf T}y\\). Thus feasible constraint multipliers are exactly feasible variables of the associated dual program.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonnegative multiplier weights each primal inequality; the multipliers satisfying the dual inequalities are precisely the feasible dual variables.
assumptions_latex: \\(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n},\ b\in\mathbb R^m,\ c\in\mathbb R^n\\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \\(y\ge0,\ A^{\mathsf T}y\ge c\iff y\text{ is dual feasible}\\)

notation.meaning: multiplier of the ith primal inequality

knowledge_statements.title: Variable–Multiplier Identification

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \\(P=\max\{c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax\le b,\ x\ge0\}\\), assigning a nonnegative multiplier \\(y_i\\) to each row \\(a_i^{\mathsf T}x\le b_i\\) produces the dual program \\(D=\min\{b^{\mathsf T}y:A^{\mathsf T}y\ge c,\ y\ge0\}\\). Consequently, the vector of primal constraint multipliers and the vector of dual decision variables are the same mathematical object; their two names indicate their Lagrangian and optimization roles.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each primal constraint multiplier is the corresponding dual decision variable, with sign and feasibility restrictions determined by the primal constraint convention.
assumptions_latex: \\(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n},\ b\in\mathbb R^m,\ c\in\mathbb R^n\\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \\((y_1,\ldots,y_m)=\text{primal constraint-multiplier vector}=\text{dual variable vector}\\)

children.title: Primal Slacks

knowledge_statements.title: Primal Slacks
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Row slacks for a canonical primal system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a vector \\(x\in\mathbb R^n\\) subject to \\(Ax\le b\\), its primal slack vector is \\(s=b-Ax\in\mathbb R^m\\). Componentwise, \\(s_i=b_i-a_i^{\mathsf T}x\\) measures the unused amount in the ith inequality. The row inequalities hold exactly when \\(s\ge0\\), and the ith inequality is active exactly when \\(s_i=0\\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Primal slack is the nonnegative residual between each inequality's right-hand side and its achieved left-hand side.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \\(Ax\le b\iff s=b-Ax\ge0\\)

notation.meaning: ith row of the constraint matrix

children.title: Dual Slacks

knowledge_statements.title: Dual Slacks
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Column slacks for the canonical dual inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a dual vector \(y\in\mathbb R^m\) subject to \(A^{\mathsf T}y\ge c\), its dual slack vector is \(r=A^{\mathsf T}y-c\in\mathbb R^n\). Componentwise, \(r_j=a_j^{\mathsf T}y-c_j\). The dual inequalities hold exactly when \(r\ge0\), and the jth dual inequality is active exactly when \(r_j=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dual slack is the nonnegative residual of each dual inequality; a zero component identifies an active dual inequality.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(A^{\mathsf T}y\ge c\iff r=A^{\mathsf T}y-c\ge0\)

notation.meaning: jth column of the constraint matrix

children.title: Complementary Slack Pairing

knowledge_statements.title: Complementary Slack Pairing
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Componentwise complementarity and the primal-dual gap identity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \\(x\\) and \\(y\\) be feasible for \\(P=\max\{c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax\le b,\ x\ge0\}\\) and its dual. With \\(s=b-Ax\\) and \\(r=A^{\mathsf T}y-c\\), the gap satisfies \\[b^{\mathsf T}y-c^{\mathsf T}x=y^{\mathsf T}s+x^{\mathsf T}r.\] Hence the feasible pair has equal objective values exactly when \\(y_i s_i=0\\) for every row and \\(x_j r_j=0\\) for every column. These are the complementary slack pairs.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Optimality pairs each multiplier with its primal slack and each primal variable with its dual slack; every paired product must vanish.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \\(b^{\mathsf T}y=c^{\mathsf T}x\iff y_i s_i=0\ \forall i,\ x_j r_j=0\ \forall j\\)

children.title: Reduced Costs

knowledge_statements.title: Reduced Costs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reduced costs under the canonical maximization convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a multiplier vector \\(y\in\mathbb R^m\\), the reduced cost of primal variable \\(x_j\\) is \\(\bar c_j=c_j-a_j^{\mathsf T}y\\), and \\(\bar c=c-A^{\mathsf T}y\\). For a simplex basis \\(B\\) with \\(y=B^{-\mathsf T}c_B\\), this becomes \\(\bar c_j=c_j-c_B^{\mathsf T}B^{-1}a_j\\). Under the maximization convention, dual feasibility is equivalent to \\(\bar c\le0\\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A reduced cost is an objective coefficient minus the value imputed to its column by the constraint multipliers.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \\(A^{\mathsf T}y\ge c\iff \bar c=c-A^{\mathsf T}y\le0\\)

notation.meaning: jth column of the constraint matrix

knowledge_statements.title: Basis Multipliers
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Simplex multipliers induced by a nonsingular primal basis.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \\(B\in\mathbb R^{m\times m}\\) be a nonsingular basis matrix and let \\(c_B\\) contain the corresponding objective coefficients. The basis-multiplier vector is the unique \\(y\\) satisfying \\(B^{\mathsf T}y=c_B\\), namely \\(y=B^{-\mathsf T}c_B\\). Equivalently, \\(y^{\mathsf T}=c_B^{\mathsf T}B^{-1}\\). It assigns multiplier values to the primal rows and generates every reduced cost through \\(\bar c_j=c_j-a_j^{\mathsf T}y\\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Basis multipliers are obtained by pricing the basic columns so their reduced costs vanish; they then determine all other reduced costs.
assumptions_latex: \\(B\text{ is a nonsingular }m\times m\text{ submatrix of }A\\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \\(y=B^{-\mathsf T}c_B\\)

children.title: Reduced-Cost–Multiplier Linkage
children.top_down_role: Structural connection between basis multipliers and reduced-cost information.

knowledge_statements.title: Reduced-Cost–Multiplier Linkage
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Columnwise linkage between Lagrangian coefficients and simplex reduced costs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \\(L(x,y)=c^{\mathsf T}x+y^{\mathsf T}(b-Ax)\\), collecting the coefficient of \\(x_j\\) gives \\[L(x,y)=b^{\mathsf T}y+\sum_{j=1}^n\bigl(c_j-a_j^{\mathsf T}y\bigr)x_j.\] Therefore the reduced-cost vector generated by multipliers \\(y\\) is \\(\bar c=c-A^{\mathsf T}y\\). If \\(y=B^{-\mathsf T}c_B\\), then basic reduced costs vanish, and dual feasibility is equivalent to every reduced cost being nonpositive.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reduced costs are exactly the coefficients left on primal variables after the constraint multipliers are inserted into the Lagrangian.
assumptions_latex: \\(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n},\ c\in\mathbb R^n,\ y\in\mathbb R^m\\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \\(\bar c_j=c_j-a_j^{\mathsf T}y\quad(j=1,\ldots,n)\\)

knowledge_statements.title: Dual Feasible Rays
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Recession directions of the canonical dual feasible polyhedron.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \\(D=\min\{b^{\mathsf T}y:A^{\mathsf T}y\ge c,\ y\ge0\}\\), a dual feasible ray direction is a nonzero vector \\(d\in\mathbb R^m\\) satisfying \\(d\ge0\\) and \\(A^{\mathsf T}d\ge0\\). If \\(y^0\\) is dual feasible, then \\(y^0+td\\) is dual feasible for every \\(t\ge0\\). Along this ray the objective equals \\(b^{\mathsf T}y^0+t b^{\mathsf T}d\\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A dual feasible ray is a nonzero recession direction that preserves every dual constraint when added with any nonnegative step length.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \\(d\ge0,\ A^{\mathsf T}d\ge0\implies y^0+td\text{ is dual feasible for all }t\ge0\\)

children.title: Certificate Rays

knowledge_statements.title: Certificate Rays
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Farkas-type dual rays certifying primal infeasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the primal system \(Ax\le b,\ x\ge0\), a certificate ray is a vector \(d\in\mathbb R^m\) satisfying \(d\ge0\), \(A^{\mathsf T}d\ge0\), and \(b^{\mathsf T}d<0\). These directly checkable conditions certify that the primal system has no feasible point. Every positive multiple \(\alpha d\), where \(\alpha>0\), represents the same certificate ray.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonnegative dual recession direction with negative right-hand-side pairing is a scalable, directly checkable certificate that the primal system is infeasible.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(d\ge0,\ A^{\mathsf T}d\ge0,\ b^{\mathsf T}d<0\implies \{x\in\mathbb R^n:x\ge0,\ Ax\le b\}=\varnothing\)

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Completeness of the certificate-ray family for nonnegative solutions of the stated inequality system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Exactly one of the following systems is solvable:
\[
\text{(i) }x\ge0,\ Ax\le b;\qquad \text{(ii) }d\ge0,\ A^{\mathsf T}d\ge0,\ b^{\mathsf T}d<0.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The nonnegative inequality system is infeasible exactly when it admits a certificate ray of the stated form.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\{x\ge0:Ax\le b\}=\varnothing\iff \exists d\ge0:\ A^{\mathsf T}d\ge0,\ b^{\mathsf T}d<0\)

knowledge_statements.title: Ray Certification Roles
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distinguishes recession evidence from infeasibility certification.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \\(d\ne0\\) satisfy \\(d\ge0\\) and \\(A^{\mathsf T}d\ge0\\). Its certification role is determined by \\(b^{\mathsf T}d\\). If \\(b^{\mathsf T}d<0\\), it certifies infeasibility of \\(Ax\le b,\ x\ge0\\) and makes every nonempty dual feasible ray \\(y^0+td\\) unbounded below. If \\(b^{\mathsf T}d=0\\), it only exhibits a constant-objective recession direction; if \\(b^{\mathsf T}d>0\\), it is an objective-increasing recession direction. Neither latter case alone certifies primal infeasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A dual recession ray certifies primal infeasibility only when its objective slope is negative; zero or positive slopes merely describe recession geometry.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \\(b^{\mathsf T}d<0\iff d\text{ has the dual-ray infeasibility-certificate role}\\)

children.title: Dual-of-the-Dual Principle
children.top_down_role: The involutive relationship between consistently represented primal and dual programs.

knowledge_statements.title: Dual-of-the-Dual Principle
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional LP dualization with consistent max/min and sign conventions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P=\max\{c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax\le b,\ x\ge0\}\), and let \(\mathcal D\) denote the LP dualization operation under fixed max/min, inequality-sense, and variable-sign conventions. Then \(\mathcal D(P)=\min\{b^{\mathsf T}y:A^{\mathsf T}y\ge c,\ y\ge0\}\), and applying \(\mathcal D\) again recovers \(P\). Thus finite-dimensional LP dualization is involutive under a consistent representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dualizing a consistently represented finite-dimensional linear program twice recovers the original program under the canonical identification of its data.

children.title: Duals of Equivalent Reformulations
children.top_down_role: The effect of slack conversion, variable splitting, redundant structure, and scaling on dual presentation.

knowledge_statements.title: Duals of Equivalent Reformulations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Covers standard equivalence-preserving LP transformations and the induced changes in dual variables and objective scales.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P\) and \(\widetilde P\) be LP formulations related by a bijective variable substitution with the feasible domain transformed accordingly, positive row scaling, positive objective scaling, slack conversion, variable splitting, or addition of a redundant constraint. Replacing an equality by two opposite inequalities represents its unrestricted multiplier as the difference of two nonnegative multipliers. Adding a nonnegative slack converts the multiplier sign rule into the corresponding dual constraint, and splitting \(x_j=x_j^+-x_j^-\) converts the associated dual inequality into an equality. Scaling primal row \(i\) by \(\alpha>0\) maps its multiplier \(y_i\) to \(y_i/\alpha\). Adding a redundant primal constraint preserves the optimal value but may create additional or nonunique dual multiplier representations. Transformations that leave the primal objective unchanged preserve corresponding dual bounds and the dual optimal value; scaling the objective by \(\beta>0\) instead scales the corresponding bounds and optimal value by \(\beta\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Equivalent reformulations induce corresponding changes in dual multipliers and preserve dual bounds when the objective is unchanged. Positive objective scaling scales, rather than preserves, the numerical bounds and optimal value, while redundant constraints may add dual representations or nonuniqueness.
assumptions_latex: Each reformulation uses a bijective domain transformation, positive row or objective scaling, slack conversion, variable splitting, or a genuinely redundant constraint.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Objective-preserving reformulations have corresponding dual bounds and the same optimal value; scaling the objective by \(\beta>0\) scales those quantities by \(\beta\).

children.title: Lagrangian Origin of the LP Dual
children.top_down_role: The multiplier interpretation connecting algebraic LP dualization to Lagrangian duality.

knowledge_statements.title: Lagrangian Origin of the LP Dual
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uses the standard equality-form minimization primal with nonnegative variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb{R}^m\), and \(c\in\mathbb{R}^n\). For \(P=\min\{c^Tx:Ax=b,\ x\geq0\}\), attach the unrestricted multiplier \(y\in\mathbb{R}^m\) to \(b-Ax=0\). The Lagrangian is \(L(x,y)=b^Ty+(c-A^Ty)^Tx\), and its dual function is \(g(y)=b^Ty\) when \(A^Ty\leq c\) and \(g(y)=-\infty\) otherwise. Consequently, the Lagrangian dual \(\max_{y\in\mathbb{R}^m}g(y)\) is exactly \(D=\max\{b^Ty:A^Ty\leq c\}\). Algebraic dual variables are therefore constraint multipliers, and dual feasibility is the condition that makes the Lagrangian infimum finite.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For an equality-form minimization LP with nonnegative variables, its Lagrangian dual is exactly the usual algebraic LP dual; the dual variables are constraint multipliers.
assumptions_latex: \(P=\min\{c^Tx:Ax=b,\ x\geq0\}\) is a finite-dimensional linear program.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The Lagrangian dual is \(\max\{b^Ty:A^Ty\leq c\}\), exactly the algebraic LP dual.

children.title: Objective-Bound Role
children.top_down_role: The use of feasible dual objects as global bounds on feasible primal values.

knowledge_statements.title: Objective-Bound Role
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Weak-duality bound for an equality-form minimization primal and its maximization dual.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb{R}^m\), and \(c\in\mathbb{R}^n\). Consider \(P=\min\{c^Tx:Ax=b,\ x\geq0\}\) and \(D=\max\{b^Ty:A^Ty\leq c\}\). For every primal-feasible \(x\in\mathbb{R}^n\) and dual-feasible \(y\in\mathbb{R}^m\), \(b^Ty\leq c^Tx\). Hence a dual-feasible multiplier \(y\), together with verification of \(A^Ty\leq c\), certifies the global lower bound \(b^Ty\) on every feasible primal objective value and on \(p^*=\inf\{c^Tx:Ax=b,\ x\geq0\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every feasible dual solution supplies a verifiable global lower bound on every feasible objective value and on the infimum of the minimization primal.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every dual-feasible value is a global lower bound: \(b^Ty\leq c^Tx\), hence \(b^Ty\leq p^*\).

children.title: Duality-Gap Role
children.top_down_role: The comparison framework underlying primal-dual gap measurements.

knowledge_statements.title: Duality-Gap Role
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the feasible-pair gap and its role as an exact optimality certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb{R}^m\), and \(c\in\mathbb{R}^n\). For \(P=\min\{c^Tx:Ax=b,\ x\geq0\}\) and \(D=\max\{b^Ty:A^Ty\leq c\}\), let \(x\in\mathbb{R}^n\) and \(y\in\mathbb{R}^m\) be feasible and define \(s=c-A^Ty\geq0\). The primal-dual gap is \(G(x,y)=c^Tx-b^Ty=x^Ts\geq0\). If \(p^*\) and \(d^*\) denote the primal and dual optimal values, respectively, then \(0\leq c^Tx-p^*\leq G(x,y)\) and \(0\leq d^*-b^Ty\leq G(x,y)\). In particular, \(G(x,y)=0\) certifies that \(x\) and \(y\) are optimal.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The feasible primal-dual objective gap is nonnegative, bounds each feasible point's objective suboptimality, and certifies mutual optimality when it is zero.
assumptions_latex: \(x\in\mathbb{R}^n\) is primal feasible and \(y\in\mathbb{R}^m\) is dual feasible for the stated primal-dual pair.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The gap satisfies \(G(x,y)\geq0\); moreover, \(G(x,y)=0\) certifies that both points are optimal.

children.title: Status-Implication Role
children.top_down_role: The one-way relationships between feasibility, objective unboundedness, and opposite-side infeasibility.

knowledge_statements.title: Status-Implication Role
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Records the one-way status implications supplied by weak duality and notes that their converses do not follow.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb{R}^m\), and \(c\in\mathbb{R}^n\), and consider \(P=\min\{c^Tx:Ax=b,\ x\geq0\}\) and \(D=\max\{b^Ty:A^Ty\leq c\}\). Weak duality implies that if \(P\) is feasible and unbounded below, then \(D\) is infeasible, and if \(D\) is feasible and unbounded above, then \(P\) is infeasible. Equivalently, feasibility of either side rules out objective unboundedness of the opposite side. Neither converse follows from weak duality: infeasibility of one side alone does not establish unboundedness of the other, and both programs can be infeasible.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Feasible unboundedness on either side forces opposite-side infeasibility, but infeasibility alone does not imply that the other side is unbounded; both sides can be infeasible.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Unboundedness of either feasible side implies infeasibility of the opposite side; opposite-side infeasibility alone does not imply unboundedness.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: LP Strong Duality and Unboundedness–Infeasibility Alternatives
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strong duality for the stated standard-form primal LP and its dual, including attainment and the two directional unboundedness–infeasibility implications.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(P=\min\{c^Tx:Ax=b,\ x\geq0\}\) and \(D=\max\{b^T\lambda:A^T\lambda\leq c\}\). If either \(P\) or \(D\) has an attained finite solution, then the other also has an attained finite solution and their optimal objective values are equal. If \(P\) is unbounded below, then \(D\) is infeasible; if \(D\) is unbounded above, then \(P\) is infeasible.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For the standard-form primal linear program and its dual, an attained finite optimum on either side guarantees an attained finite optimum on the other side with the same value. If the primal is unbounded below, the dual is infeasible; if the dual is unbounded above, the primal is infeasible.

knowledge_statements.title: Zero Duality Gap
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Value-equality component of finite-dimensional LP strong duality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb{R}^m\), and \(c\in\mathbb{R}^n\). For \(P=\min\{c^Tx:Ax=b,\ x\geq0\}\) and \(D=\max\{b^Ty:A^Ty\leq c\}\), suppose \(P\) is feasible and has a finite infimum. Strong duality provides optimizers \(x^*\in\mathbb{R}^n\) and \(y^*\in\mathbb{R}^m\) with \(c^Tx^*=b^Ty^*\). Thus the attained optimal values \(p^*=c^Tx^*\) and \(d^*=b^Ty^*\) satisfy \(p^*=d^*\), equivalently \(p^*-d^*=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: In the feasible finite-optimum LP regime, the attained primal and dual optimal values coincide, so the optimal duality gap is zero.
assumptions_latex: \(P=\min\{c^Tx:Ax=b,\ x\geq0\}\) is feasible and has a finite infimum.

knowledge_statements.title: Primal Attainment
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Attainment of a finite linear minimum over a nonempty polyhedron.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb{R}^m\), and \(c\in\mathbb{R}^n\), and define \(X=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:Ax=b,\ x\geq0\}\). If \(X\neq\varnothing\) and \(p^*=\inf_{x\in X}c^Tx\) is finite, then there exists \(x^*\in X\) such that \(c^Tx^*=p^*\). Thus a feasible finite-dimensional LP cannot have a finite but unattained infimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A linear objective with a finite infimum on a nonempty finite-dimensional polyhedron attains that infimum at a feasible primal solution.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: There exists \(x^*\in X\) satisfying \(c^Tx^*=\inf_{x\in X}c^Tx\).

children.top_down_role: Existence of a dual optimizer within the finite-optimum regime.

knowledge_statements.title: Dual Attainment
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dual attainment implied by finite-dimensional LP strong duality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb{R}^m\), and \(c\in\mathbb{R}^n\). Suppose \(P=\min\{c^Tx:Ax=b,\ x\geq0\}\) is feasible and has finite optimal value \(p^*\). For its dual \(D=\max\{b^Ty:A^Ty\leq c\}\), there exists \(y^*\in\mathbb{R}^m\) satisfying \(A^Ty^*\leq c\) at which the dual supremum is attained, and \(b^Ty^*=p^*\). Thus an actual dual multiplier realizes the sharp global lower bound on the primal objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When the primal LP is feasible with finite optimum, a dual-feasible multiplier attains the dual maximum and matches the primal value.
assumptions_latex: The primal optimal value \(p^*\) is finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: There exists \(y^*\in\mathbb{R}^m\) with \(A^Ty^*\leq c\) and \(b^Ty^*=p^*\).

children.title: Attainment Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Modeling regimes separating attained LP optima from broader nonattainment phenomena.

assumptions_latex: The primal and dual are a finite-dimensional LP pair under consistent extended-value conventions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Finite optimal values are attained and equal; absence of an optimizer occurs only through infeasibility or objective unboundedness, not finite nonattainment.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separates finite LP attainment from infeasible and unbounded status regimes.

source_refs.locator: 4. The Strong Duality Theorem p. 63

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a finite-dimensional linear program over a polyhedron, feasibility together with a finite optimal value implies attainment. Therefore finite nonattainment, which can occur in more general optimization problems, is excluded for LPs. The boundary cases are instead status failures: an empty feasible set yields infeasibility, while a nonempty feasible set with objective values decreasing without bound yields unboundedness below for a minimization problem. In the finite regime, both primal and dual optimizers exist and their values agree. If one side is feasible and objective-unbounded, weak duality forces the opposite side to be infeasible; both sides may also be infeasible.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Finite-dimensional LPs cannot have a feasible, finite, unattained optimum; optimizer absence arises through infeasibility or objective unboundedness, with weak duality restricting opposite-side status.
knowledge_statements.title: Attainment Boundaries

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scalar standard-form examples separating unboundedness, opposite-side infeasibility, and simultaneous infeasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(P=\min\{cx:Ax=b,\ x\ge0\}\) and \(D=\max\{by:A^{\mathsf T}y\le c\}\), the scalar data give the following sharp status examples:
\[(A,b,c)=(0,0,-1):\quad P\text{ is unbounded below and }D\text{ is infeasible};\]
\[(A,b,c)=(0,1,0):\quad P\text{ is infeasible and }D\text{ is unbounded above};\]
\[(A,b,c)=(0,1,-1):\quad P\text{ and }D\text{ are both infeasible}.\]
Thus infeasibility of one side alone does not determine whether the opposite side is unbounded or infeasible, whereas feasible unboundedness forces opposite-side infeasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Three scalar LPs realize primal-unbounded/dual-infeasible, primal-infeasible/dual-unbounded, and simultaneous-infeasibility statuses.
assumptions_latex: The primal and dual use the displayed equality-form minimization convention.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: All three stated boundary-status combinations occur in finite-dimensional linear programming.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Any finite-dimensional LP with mixed row senses, free or sign-restricted variables, and finite lower or upper bounds can be converted to canonical form by sign changes, slack variables, translations, and variable splitting. Dualizing the canonical form and eliminating the introduced quantities yields the general-form rules: equality rows have unrestricted multipliers; inequality rows impose the sign appropriate to the primal optimization direction; free primal variables produce dual equalities; sign-restricted variables produce corresponding dual inequalities; and explicit bounds contribute multiplier terms. If the primal has a finite optimum, these transformations preserve feasibility and objective values, and the resulting general-form dual has an attained optimum equal to the primal optimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Canonical strong duality extends to mixed constraints, free or signed variables, and finite bounds when dual multiplier signs and constraint senses are matched correctly.

children.title: Foundational Routes to Strong Duality
children.top_down_role: The basis, alternative, separation, and elimination perspectives connecting strong duality to other LP foundations.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Supporting-hyperplane foundation for equality-form strong duality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(P=\min\{c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax=b,\ x\ge0\}\), define the polyhedral epigraphical image
\[Q=\{(u,t):\exists x\ge0,\ Ax=u,\ c^{\mathsf T}x\le t\}.\]
If \(P\) is feasible with finite value \(p^*\), the boundary point \((b,p^*)\) admits a supporting hyperplane of the form \(t\ge y^{\mathsf T}u\). Its coefficients satisfy \(A^{\mathsf T}y\le c\) and \(b^{\mathsf T}y=p^*\), so the separator is an optimal dual multiplier.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A supporting hyperplane to the polyhedral value epigraph at the finite optimum produces a dual-feasible multiplier attaining the primal value.
assumptions_latex: The equality-form primal is finite-dimensional, feasible, and has finite value \(p^*\).
\(Q\) is the displayed polyhedral epigraphical image.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: There exists \(y\) with \(A^{\mathsf T}y\le c\) and \(b^{\mathsf T}y=p^*\).

notation.meaning: Polyhedral image encoding feasible right-hand sides and objective upper levels.

knowledge_statements.title: Polyhedral-Separation Route to Strong Duality

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact linear-elimination foundation for equality-form strong duality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a finite-dimensional equality-form primal, exact elimination of the primal variables from the linear systems expressing feasibility together with an objective-level bound produces the multiplier inequalities \(A^{\mathsf T}y\le c\) and the bound \(b^{\mathsf T}y\). At the finite optimal level \(p^*\), the closed polyhedral projection yields a multiplier satisfying \(b^{\mathsf T}y=p^*\); hence the eliminated system is the dual feasibility system with an attained matching value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact projection or elimination of the primal-variable system yields the dual multiplier inequalities and, at the finite optimum, a matching dual value.
assumptions_latex: The primal system is finite-dimensional and polyhedral.
The equality-form primal is feasible with finite optimal value \(p^*\).
Elimination is exact and retains all projected inequalities.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The eliminated multiplier system contains some \(y\) with \(A^{\mathsf T}y\le c\) and \(b^{\mathsf T}y=p^*\).
knowledge_statements.title: Elimination Route to Dual Multipliers

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Basis foundation for equality-form strong duality after redundant equality rows are removed.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(\min\{c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax=b,\ x\ge0\}\) with \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) of full row rank. If the problem is feasible with finite optimum, there is an optimal basis \(B\) and a vector \(y\) satisfying \(A_B^{\mathsf T}y=c_B\), \(A_N^{\mathsf T}y\le c_N\), and \(b^{\mathsf T}y=c^{\mathsf T}x^*\). Thus optimal-basis reduced-cost conditions provide an attained dual optimum and the strong-duality equality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An optimal primal basis yields dual multipliers from the basic costs; nonnegative reduced costs give dual feasibility and equality with the basic primal value.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) has full row rank.
The equality-form primal is feasible and has a finite optimal value.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: An optimal basis supplies \(y\) with \(A^{\mathsf T}y\le c\) and \(b^{\mathsf T}y=c^{\mathsf T}x^*\).

notation.meaning: Basic and nonbasic column index sets.
Multiplier equations determined by the basic costs.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a feasible LP \(P=\min\{c^Tx:Ax=b,\ x\geq0\}\) with finite optimum, strong duality can be grounded in several equivalent finite-dimensional foundations. An optimal-basis argument derives multipliers from reduced-cost optimality; a theorem of alternatives certifies the impossibility of a strictly better objective level; separation supplies a supporting hyperplane to the relevant polyhedral image; and elimination projects the primal inequalities into precisely the dual feasibility conditions. Each route yields or certifies a vector \(y^*\) satisfying \(A^Ty^*\leq c\) and \(b^Ty^*=c^Tx^*\) for some primal optimizer \(x^*\). These are alternative foundations for the same value-and-attainment conclusion.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Optimal bases, alternatives, polyhedral separation, and elimination provide distinct foundations that all produce the same strong-duality equality and optimal multipliers.

knowledge_statements.title: Standard-Form Complementarity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Complementary slackness for an equality-form primal minimization problem and its slack-form dual.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let the primal problem be 
\[\min\{c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax=b,\ x\ge 0\}\]
and let its dual be
\[\max\{b^{\mathsf T}y:A^{\mathsf T}y+s=c,\ s\ge 0\}.\]
If 
\(x\) and 
\((y,s)\) are primal and dual feasible, respectively, then they are both optimal if and only if
\[x_j s_j=0\quad\text{for every }j.\]
Equivalently, 
\(x^{\mathsf T}s=0\). Thus every positive primal variable has zero dual slack, and every positive dual slack corresponds to a zero primal variable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible standard-form primal-dual pair is optimal exactly when every primal variable is complementary to its corresponding nonnegative dual slack.
assumptions_latex: \(x\) and \((y,s)\) satisfy the displayed primal and dual feasibility systems.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x\) and \((y,s)\) are optimal if and only if \(x_js_j=0\) for all \(j\).

children.title: General-Form Complementarity
children.top_down_role: Complementarity across mixed constraint senses, variable signs, and explicit bounds.

knowledge_statements.title: General-Form Complementarity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Multiplier complementarity for finite-dimensional linear equalities, inequalities, and finite lower or upper bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(c\in\mathbb R^n\), \(E\in\mathbb R^{p\times n}\), \(d\in\mathbb R^p\), \(G\in\mathbb R^{q\times n}\), and \(h\in\mathbb R^q\). Let \(\ell\in(\mathbb R\cup\{-\infty\})^n\) and \(u\in(\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\})^n\), and define \(L=\{j:\ell_j> -\infty\}\) and \(U=\{j:u_j<+\infty\}\). Consider
\[\min\{c^{\mathsf T}x:Ex=d,\ Gx\le h,\ \ell_j\le x_j\ (j\in L),\ x_j\le u_j\ (j\in U)\}.\]
A primal-feasible \(x\in\mathbb R^n\) and multipliers \(y\in\mathbb R^p\), \(\lambda\in\mathbb R_+^q\), \(\alpha\in\mathbb R_+^L\), and \(\beta\in\mathbb R_+^U\) constitute an optimal primal-dual pair if and only if
\[c+E^{\mathsf T}y+G^{\mathsf T}\lambda-\sum_{j\in L}\alpha_j e_j+\sum_{j\in U}\beta_j e_j=0\]
and
\[\lambda_i(h_i-(Gx)_i)=0\ (i=1,\ldots,q),\quad \alpha_j(x_j-\ell_j)=0\ (j\in L),\quad \beta_j(u_j-x_j)=0\ (j\in U).\]
Inequalities of the opposite sense may be multiplied by \(-1\) before applying this convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a finite-dimensional general-form LP, primal feasibility, nonnegative inequality and bound multipliers, stationarity, and the corresponding complementary products characterize an optimal primal-dual pair.
assumptions_latex: \(E\in\mathbb R^{p\times n}\), \(G\in\mathbb R^{q\times n}\), \(c\in\mathbb R^n\), \(d\in\mathbb R^p\), and \(h\in\mathbb R^q\).
\(L\) and \(U\) index the finite lower and upper bounds, respectively.
The displayed primal point and multipliers satisfy their stated domain and sign restrictions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Primal-dual optimality is equivalent to the displayed stationarity and complementary-product conditions.

notation.meaning: The j-th coordinate vector in real n-space.
Indices having finite lower and upper bounds, respectively.
Equality, inequality, lower-bound, and upper-bound multipliers.

knowledge_statements.title: Complementarity-Based Optimality Characterization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Complete and directly checkable optimality certificate for a standard-form primal-dual pair.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For the primal-dual pair
\[\min\{c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax=b,\ x\ge0\},\qquad \max\{b^{\mathsf T}y:A^{\mathsf T}y+s=c,\ s\ge0\},\]
a triple 
\((x,y,s)\) is an optimality certificate if and only if
\[Ax=b,\quad x\ge0,\quad A^{\mathsf T}y+s=c,\quad s\ge0,\quad x_js_j=0\ \text{for all }j.\]
These relations are finitely verifiable. They imply the matching objective values 
\(c^{\mathsf T}x=b^{\mathsf T}y\), while every optimal primal-dual solution pair satisfies them.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Primal feasibility, dual feasibility, and componentwise complementarity form a necessary and sufficient, finitely checkable certificate of LP optimality.
assumptions_latex: \(A\), \(b\), and \(c\) are finite real data of compatible dimensions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed feasibility and complementarity relations hold exactly for optimal primal-dual triples.

notation.meaning: Primal variables, equality multipliers, and dual slacks.

Each condition, together with primal and dual feasibility, certifies optimality of both solutions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a feasible standard-form primal-dual pair, the duality gap equals total complementarity; zero gap, zero scalar complementarity, and componentwise complementarity are equivalent certificates.

knowledge_statements.title: Complementary Activity Patterns
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Indexwise activity restrictions shared by optimal solutions of a standard-form primal-dual pair.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let 
\(X^*\) be the primal optimal set and 
\(D^*\) the set of dual-optimal pairs for the standard-form primal-dual problems. For every 
\(x\in X^*\) and 
\((y,s)\in D^*\),
\[x_js_j=0\quad\text{for all }j.\]
Consequently, if some 
\(x\in X^*\) has 
\(x_j>0\), then every dual optimum has 
\(s_j=0\); if some dual optimum has 
\(s_j>0\), then every primal optimum has 
\(x_j=0\). Thus positivity on either optimal face forces universal inactivity of its complementary coordinate on the opposite face.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A coordinate positive somewhere on one optimal face forces its complementary coordinate to vanish throughout the opposite optimal face.
assumptions_latex: Both standard-form primal and dual optimal sets are nonempty.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_js_j=0\) for every \(x\in X^*\), every \((y,s)\in D^*\), and every \(j\).

knowledge_statements.title: Optimal-Face Geometry
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Facial structure of primal and dual solution sets exposed by their objective functions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let 
\(P=\{x:Ax=b,\ x\ge0\}\) and 
\(D=\{(y,s):A^{\mathsf T}y+s=c,\ s\ge0\}\). If the common finite optimal value is 
\(v\), then
\[X^*=P\cap\{x:c^{\mathsf T}x=v\},\qquad D^*=D\cap\{(y,s):b^{\mathsf T}y=v\}\]
are exposed faces of 
\(P\) and 
\(D\), respectively. Moreover, every point of 
\(X^*\) is complementary to every point of 
\(D^*\):
\[x^{\mathsf T}s=0\quad\text{for all }x\in X^*,\ (y,s)\in D^*.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The primal and dual solution sets are exposed faces, and every point of either optimal face is complementary to every point of the other.
assumptions_latex: The standard-form primal and dual attain the same finite optimal value \(v\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(X^*\) and \(D^*\) are exposed faces satisfying universal cross-complementarity.

children.title: Complementary-Face Correspondence
children.top_down_role: Relationship between complementary activity patterns and paired optimal faces.

knowledge_statements.title: Complementary-Face Correspondence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coordinate-zero correspondence between the primal and dual optimal faces in standard form.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For nonempty optimal faces \(X^*\) and \(D^*\), define
\[I=\{j:x_j=0\text{ for every }x\in X^*\},\qquad J=\{j:s_j=0\text{ for every }(y,s)\in D^*\}.\]
Universal complementarity gives
\[j\notin I\Longrightarrow j\in J,\qquad j\notin J\Longrightarrow j\in I.\]
Consequently,
\[I\cup J=\{1,\ldots,n\}.\]
Thus a coordinate that is positive at some point of one optimal face is fixed at zero throughout the opposite optimal face. The intersection \(I\cap J\) consists of coordinates fixed at zero on both optimal faces. If a strictly complementary optimal pair exists, then
\[I\cap J=\varnothing,\]
so \(I\) and \(J\) partition \(\{1,\ldots,n\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Coordinates that can be positive on either optimal face are fixed at zero on the opposite face. The two fixed-zero index sets cover all coordinates and, under strict complementarity, form a partition.
assumptions_latex: The standard-form primal and dual optimal faces \(X^*\) and \(D^*\) are nonempty.
The partition conclusion additionally assumes the existence of a strictly complementary optimal pair.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(I\cup J=\{1,\ldots,n\}\); under strict complementarity, additionally \(I\cap J=\varnothing\).

notation.meaning: Coordinates fixed at zero throughout the primal optimal face.
Slack coordinates fixed at zero throughout the dual optimal face.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp fixed-zero partition obtained for nonempty finite-dimensional standard-form optimal faces using strict-complementarity existence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X^*\) and \(D^*\) be nonempty optimal sets for a finite-dimensional standard-form primal-dual pair, and define \[I=\{j:x_j=0\ \text{for every }x\in X^*\},\qquad J=\{j:s_j=0\ \text{for every }(y,s)\in D^*\}.\] Then \[I\cup J=\{1,\ldots,n\},\qquad I\cap J=\varnothing.\] Equivalently, for each coordinate exactly one of the following holds: some primal optimum has \(x_j>0\), or some dual optimum has \(s_j>0\).

knowledge_statements.title: Basis-Derived Dual Solutions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dual multipliers and slacks recovered algebraically from a nonsingular primal basis.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For 
\(\min\{c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax=b,\ x\ge0\}\), let 
\(B\) index 
\(m\) linearly independent columns of 
\(A\), with basis matrix 
\(A_B\). The basis-derived multiplier is the unique vector
\[y=A_B^{-\mathsf T}c_B,\]
and its dual slack vector is
\[s=c-A^{\mathsf T}y.\]
It satisfies 
\(s_B=0\), while
\[s_N=c_N-A_N^{\mathsf T}A_B^{-\mathsf T}c_B\]
is the reduced-cost vector. Hence the basis-derived pair 
\((y,s)\) is dual feasible exactly when 
\(s_N\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonsingular primal basis determines unique dual multipliers; its nonbasic dual slacks are exactly the reduced costs.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(y=A_B^{-\mathsf T}c_B\), \(s_B=0\), and dual feasibility is equivalent to \(s_N\ge0\).

children.title: Reduced-Cost Optimality Criteria

knowledge_statements.title: Reduced-Cost Optimality Criteria
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reduced-cost certificate for a primal-feasible basis of a standard-form minimization problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(B\) be a basis for
\[\min\{c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax=b,\ x\ge0\},\]
let \(N\) be its complementary index set, and define
\[x_B=A_B^{-1}b,\quad x_N=0,\quad y=A_B^{-\mathsf T}c_B,\quad \bar c_N=c_N-A_N^{\mathsf T}y.\]
If
\[x_B\ge0\quad\text{and}\quad \bar c_N\ge0,\]
then the associated basic feasible solution is optimal. With \(s_B=0\) and \(s_N=\bar c_N\), the basis-derived dual pair is feasible and complementary to \(x\). Thus a primal-feasible basis is a primal-dual optimal basis exactly when its nonbasic reduced costs are nonnegative. Under degeneracy, an optimal basic feasible point may also be represented by another basis having a negative reduced cost, so the sign condition is not necessary for every basis representing that point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nonnegative reduced costs certify optimality of a primal-feasible basis and characterize primal-dual optimal bases, although degeneracy can give an optimal point another representing basis that fails the sign test.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\bar c_N\ge0\) certifies optimality, and it is equivalent to dual feasibility of the basis-derived multiplier and slack.

notation.meaning: Reduced costs of the nonbasic variables.
Basic component of the associated basic solution.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Zero Reduced Cost Does Not Guarantee an Alternative Optimum
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of the converse that one zero nonbasic reduced cost necessarily yields a distinct optimal solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \[\min\{0:x_1+x_2=0,\ x_1,x_2\ge0\}.\] With basis \(B=\{1\}\), the basic solution is \(x=(0,0)\), and \(\bar c_2=0\). Nevertheless, feasibility forces \(x_1=x_2=0\), so the optimal solution is unique. A zero nonbasic reduced cost therefore does not imply an alternative optimum without a nonzero feasible zero-cost direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonbasic variable can have zero reduced cost even when the feasible and optimal solution is unique; an appropriate feasible zero-cost direction is also required.
assumptions_latex: The standard-form minimization convention is used.

notation.meaning: The basis containing the first column.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Reduced-Cost Gap Decomposition and Optimal-Support Test
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact objective-gap decomposition relative to a primal-feasible basis with nonnegative reduced costs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(B\) be a primal-feasible basis for \(\min\{c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax=b,\ x\ge0\}\), let \(x^B\) be its basic solution, and let \(y=A_B^{-\mathsf T}c_B\) and \(\bar c_N=c_N-A_N^{\mathsf T}y\ge0\). For every primal-feasible \(x\), \[c^{\mathsf T}x-c^{\mathsf T}x^B=\bar c_N^{\mathsf T}x_N.\] Hence \(x\) is optimal if and only if \(\bar c_N^{\mathsf T}x_N=0\), equivalently \(x_j=0\) for every \(j\in N\) with \(\bar c_j>0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Relative to an optimal basis, the objective gap is reduced-cost-weighted nonbasic activity; every optimum sets all positive-reduced-cost nonbasic variables to zero.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(c^{\mathsf T}x-c^{\mathsf T}x^B=\bar c_N^{\mathsf T}x_N\), and \(x\in X^*\iff\bar c_N^{\mathsf T}x_N=0\).

notation.meaning: The basic feasible solution associated with B.

knowledge_statements.title: Primal Optimal Bases
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Algebraic conditions for primal feasibility and primal-dual optimality of a standard-form column basis.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For
\[\min\{c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax=b,\ x\ge0\},\]
let \(B\) be a nonsingular column basis and \(N\) its complementary index set. The basis is primal feasible exactly when
\[A_B^{-1}b\ge0.\]
A primal-feasible basis is a primal-dual optimal basis exactly when
\[c_N-A_N^{\mathsf T}A_B^{-\mathsf T}c_B\ge0.\]
Under both inequalities, the basis-derived primal and dual solutions are feasible and complementary, so the basic primal solution is optimal. Degeneracy may allow an optimal basic feasible point to be represented by another basis that does not satisfy the reduced-cost inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A basis is primal feasible when its basic variables are nonnegative, and such a basis is primal-dual optimal when its nonbasic reduced costs are also nonnegative. Degeneracy can give an optimal point additional nonoptimal representing bases.
assumptions_latex: The LP is a finite-dimensional standard-form minimization problem.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The two inequalities characterize a primal-feasible, dual-feasible optimal basis and suffice to generate an optimal primal basic solution.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Existence of an Optimal Representing Basis
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Existence of at least one reduced-cost-compatible basis representing an optimal basic feasible solution despite possible incompatible degenerate representations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(\min\{c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax=b,\ x\ge0\}\) with \(\operatorname{rank}(A)=m\). If \(x^*\) is an optimal basic feasible solution, then some index set \(B\) of \(m\) columns satisfies \[A_B\text{ nonsingular},\quad x_N^*=0,\quad x_B^*=A_B^{-1}b\ge0,\quad c_N-A_N^{\mathsf T}A_B^{-\mathsf T}c_B\ge0.\] Other bases representing the same degenerate point may fail the reduced-cost condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every optimal basic feasible solution admits at least one representing optimal basis, although degeneracy may permit other nonoptimal basis representations of the same point.
assumptions_latex: \(x^*\) is an optimal basic feasible solution of the stated standard-form minimization problem.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists B:\ A_B\text{ is nonsingular},\ x_N^*=0,\ A_B^{-1}b\ge0,\ c_N-A_N^{\mathsf T}A_B^{-\mathsf T}c_B\ge0.\)

knowledge_statements.title: Dual Optimal Bases
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dual feasibility and joint optimality conditions induced by a standard-form column basis.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given a nonsingular column basis \(B\) with complement \(N\), define
\[y=A_B^{-\mathsf T}c_B,\qquad s_B=0,\qquad s_N=c_N-A_N^{\mathsf T}y.\]
The basis-derived pair \((y,s)\) is dual feasible exactly when
\[s_N\ge0.\]
If, in addition,
\[x_B=A_B^{-1}b\ge0,\qquad x_N=0,\]
then the basis-derived primal and dual solutions are feasible and complementary and hence are both optimal. Thus
\[s_N\ge0\quad\text{and}\quad A_B^{-1}b\ge0\]
characterize joint primal-dual optimality of the basis-derived pair. They do not characterize optimality of \(y\) alone independently of the chosen basis.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nonnegative reduced costs characterize dual feasibility of the basis-derived multiplier. Together with nonnegative basic primal variables, they characterize joint optimality of the basis-derived primal-dual pair.
assumptions_latex: The primal and dual use the standard-form minimization convention.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(s_N\ge0\) is equivalent to basis-derived dual feasibility, while \(s_N\ge0\) and \(A_B^{-1}b\ge0\) characterize joint basis-derived optimality.

notation.meaning: Nonbasic dual slacks or reduced costs.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Dual solution induced by a primal-optimal basis
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical-form primal minimization LPs and their basis-induced dual solutions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a canonical-form primal minimization problem, let \(B\) be a primal-optimal basis, so the associated basic solution is feasible and \(z_j-c_j=c_BB^{-1}a_j-c_j\le 0\) for every \(j\). Then \(w^*=c_BB^{-1}\) is dual optimal. Moreover, for \(i=1,\ldots,m\), \(w_i^*=-(z_{n+i}-c_{n+i})=-z_{n+i}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a canonical-form primal minimization problem, the multipliers obtained from any primal-optimal basis B as w*=c_B B^{-1} form a dual-optimal solution. Each component also equals the negative reduced-cost expression for the corresponding added variable: w_i*=-(z_{n+i}-c_{n+i})=-z_{n+i}.
assumptions_latex: \(B\) is a basis for a canonical-form primal minimization problem whose basic solution is primal feasible.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(w^*=c_BB^{-1}\) is dual optimal, and \(w_i^*=-(z_{n+i}-c_{n+i})=-z_{n+i}\) for \(i=1,\ldots,m\).

knowledge_statements.title: Complementary Basis Correspondence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A common basis simultaneously produces complementary primal and dual solutions when both basis-feasibility tests hold.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let 
\(B\) be a nonsingular column basis and 
\(N\) its complement. The associated pair
\[x_B=A_B^{-1}b,\quad x_N=0,\qquad y=A_B^{-\mathsf T}c_B,\quad s_B=0,\quad s_N=c_N-A_N^{\mathsf T}y\]
is automatically complementary because 
\(x_N=0\) and 
\(s_B=0\). The basis gives a complementary optimal primal-dual pair if and only if
\[x_B\ge0\quad\text{and}\quad s_N\ge0.\]
Thus primal basis feasibility and dual basis feasibility are the two halves of basis optimality. Degenerate zero basic variables or zero nonbasic slacks can allow multiple complementary bases for one optimal pair.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: One basis determines complementary primal and dual candidates; they are jointly optimal exactly when the basic variables and reduced costs are nonnegative.
assumptions_latex: The LP uses the standard-form minimization primal-dual convention.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The basis-derived pair is optimal if and only if \(A_B^{-1}b\ge0\) and \(c_N-A_N^{\mathsf T}A_B^{-\mathsf T}c_B\ge0\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Multiplier Characterization of a Valid Linear Inequality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Farkas characterization of inequalities valid on a nonempty polyhedron described by one-sided linear inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb{R}^m\), \(c\in\mathbb{R}^n\), and \(d\in\mathbb{R}\), and suppose \(P=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:Ax\le b\}\neq\varnothing\). Then \(c^{\mathsf T}x\le d\) for every \(x\in P\) if and only if there exists \(p\in\mathbb{R}^m_+\) such that \(p^{\mathsf T}A=c^{\mathsf T}\) and \(p^{\mathsf T}b\le d\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a nonempty system Ax ≤ b, an inequality cᵀx ≤ d is valid for every feasible point exactly when a nonnegative combination of the defining inequalities has left side cᵀx and right side at most d.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \bigl(\forall x\in\mathbb{R}^n,\ Ax\le b\Rightarrow c^{\mathsf T}x\le d\bigr)\iff\bigl(\exists p\in\mathbb{R}^m_+:p^{\mathsf T}A=c^{\mathsf T},\ p^{\mathsf T}b\le d\bigr).
