children.title: Primal Degeneracy in Duality
children.top_down_role: Duality effects of redundant activity and multiple bases representing a primal solution.

knowledge_statements.title: Primal Degeneracy in Duality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Basis-level primal degeneracy and its effect on dual certificates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\max\{c^\top x:Ax=b,\ x\ge0\}\) with \(\operatorname{rank}(A)=m\), a basic feasible solution \(x\) associated with a basis \(B\) is primal degenerate when \((x_B)_i=0\) for some basic index. Equivalently, more than \(n-m\) nonnegativity constraints are active at \(x\). Degeneracy permits distinct bases to represent the same primal point and permits a simplex pivot of zero step length. It does not by itself imply multiple primal optimal points or multiple dual optimal multipliers; those require positive-dimensional primal or dual optimal faces, respectively.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A primal basic solution is degenerate when a basic variable vanishes. Multiple bases may then represent one point, but neither primal nor dual nonuniqueness follows automatically.
assumptions_latex: \(B\) indexes an invertible \(m\times m\) basis matrix.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x\) is degenerate iff some component of \(x_B=B^{-1}b\) is zero.

notation.meaning: basis matrix formed from m columns of A

source_refs.locator: 6.2 Primal-Dual Relationships p. 264

source_witnesses.locator: 6.2 Primal-Dual Relationships p. 264

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Degeneracy Does Not Determine Primal or Dual Multiplicity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Parametric examples separating primal basis degeneracy from primal-solution and dual-multiplier multiplicity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(\gamma\ge0\), consider
\[
\min\{\gamma x_3:x_1+x_3=1,\ x_2-x_3=0,\ x\ge0\}.
\]
The basis formed by the columns of \(x_1,x_2\) represents the degenerate optimum \((1,0,0)\). If \(\gamma>0\), this primal optimum is unique, while the dual optimal set is \(\{(y_1,y_2):y_1=0,\ -\gamma\le y_2\le0\}\). If \(\gamma=0\), the primal optimal set is \(\{(1-t,t,t):0\le t\le1\}\), while the dual optimum is uniquely \((0,0)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: One degenerate basis family has a unique primal optimum but multiple dual optima for positive parameter values, and multiple primal optima but a unique dual optimum at zero.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Primal degeneracy implies neither primal multiplicity nor dual multiplicity.}

notation.meaning: nonnegative objective coefficient distinguishing the two multiplicity regimes

knowledge_statements.title: Degeneracy Does Not Determine Primal or Dual Multiplicity

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Degenerate Optimal Basis Obstructs Basis-Induced Strict Complementarity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Effect of primal basis degeneracy on the complementary pair generated by that same optimal basis.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\min\{c^\top x:Ax=b,\ x\ge0\}\), let \(B\) be an optimal basis, set \(x_B=B^{-1}b\), \(x_N=0\), \(y=B^{-\top}c_B\), and \(s=c-A^\top y\). If \((x_B)_i=0\) for some \(i\in B\), then \(s_i=0\) because every basic reduced cost vanishes. Hence \(x_i=s_i=0\), so the optimal pair induced by \(B\) is not strictly complementary. This does not preclude another optimal pair from being strictly complementary.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A primal-degenerate optimal basis induces an optimal pair with a zero-zero basic coordinate and therefore cannot itself be strictly complementary.
assumptions_latex: \(B\) is an optimal nonsingular basis for the displayed standard-form minimization problem.
\((x_B)_i=0\) for at least one basic index \(i\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: i\in B,\ (x_B)_i=0\Rightarrow x_i=s_i=0.
knowledge_statements.title: Degenerate Optimal Basis Obstructs Basis-Induced Strict Complementarity

children.title: Dual Degeneracy-Multiplicity Correspondence
children.top_down_role: Multiplicity of dual solutions, supporting multipliers, and shadow prices.

children.title: Dual Degeneracy
children.top_down_role: Degenerate dual basis and activity structures at optimality.

knowledge_statements.title: Dual Degeneracy
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Geometric dual degeneracy for the equality-form primal dual.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(Y=\{y\in\mathbb R^m:A^\top y\ge c\}\), and let \(y\) be a vertex of \(Y\). Its active index set is \(K(y)=\{j:A_j^\top y=c_j\}\). The vertex \(y\) is dual degenerate when its active system contains more constraints than are required to determine it, namely
\[
|K(y)|>m
\]
under the full-row-rank convention. More invariantly, dual degeneracy means \(|K(y)|>\operatorname{rank}(A_{K(y)})=m\). Thus more than one linearly independent choice of \(m\) active dual inequalities may define the same dual vertex.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A dual vertex is degenerate when more active dual inequalities occur than are needed to determine the vertex, allowing several active bases to represent it.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(y\) is dual degenerate iff \(|K(y)|>\operatorname{rank}(A_{K(y)})=m\).

notation.meaning: indices of dual inequalities active at y
columns of A indexed by the active set

children.title: Multiplier Multiplicity
children.top_down_role: Regimes containing multiple supporting multiplier vectors.

knowledge_statements.title: Multiplier Multiplicity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Set-valued certificate for nonunique optimal dual multipliers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For an optimal primal solution \(x^*\), define
\[
M(x^*)=\{y:A^\top y-c\ge0,\ b^\top y=c^\top x^*,\ x_j^*(A_j^\top y-c_j)=0\text{ for all }j\}.
\]
Every element of \(M(x^*)\) is a verifiable optimal dual multiplier by feasibility, objective equality, and complementary slackness. Multiplier multiplicity occurs exactly when \(M(x^*)\) contains two distinct points. If \(y^0,y^1\in M(x^*)\) and \(y^0\ne y^1\), their displayed constraints constitute a finite certificate of nonuniqueness; convexity then gives the entire segment between them in \(M(x^*)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two distinct dual-feasible multipliers satisfying objective equality and complementary slackness with one primal optimum certify multiplier nonuniqueness and generate a continuum of multipliers.
assumptions_latex: \(x^*\) is feasible and optimal for \(\max\{c^\top x:Ax=b,\ x\ge0\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(|M(x^*)|>1\iff\) optimal multipliers are nonunique.

notation.meaning: optimal multiplier set compatible with x-star

children.title: Shadow-Price Nonuniqueness
children.top_down_role: Ambiguity in marginal-value interpretations caused by nonunique dual solutions.

knowledge_statements.title: Shadow-Price Nonuniqueness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Interpretation of multiple dual optima as multiple marginal-value vectors.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define the right-hand-side value function \(v(\beta)=\max\{c^\top x:Ax=\beta,\ x\ge0\}\), and suppose \(v(b)\) is finite and attained. If \(Y^*(b)\) is the dual optimal set, then every \(y\in Y^*(b)\) satisfies
\[
v(\beta)\le v(b)+y^\top(\beta-b)
\]
whenever \(v(\beta)\) is finite. Hence each dual optimum is a shadow-price vector supporting the concave polyhedral value function at \(b\). When \(Y^*(b)\) is non-singleton, the shadow price is nonunique, and for every feasible direction \(h\),
\[
v'(b;h)=\min_{y\in Y^*(b)}y^\top h.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Multiple dual optima give multiple supporting shadow-price vectors. The directional marginal value selects the smallest pairing with the perturbation direction.
assumptions_latex: The primal value at \(b\) is finite and attained.
The directional value \(v'(b;h)\) is taken within the finite domain of \(v\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Y^*(b)\) non-singleton implies nonunique shadow prices, with \(v'(b;h)=\min_{y\in Y^*(b)}y^\top h\).

notation.meaning: optimal value under right-hand side beta
dual optimal multiplier set at b

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonuniqueness of the full shadow-price vector need not make every directional or coordinate marginal value ambiguous.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Y^*(b)\) be the nonempty dual optimal set. For a feasible direction \(h\), the directional marginal value is \(v'(b;h)=\min_{y\in Y^*(b)}y^\top h\). Although \(Y^*(b)\) may contain several vectors, all optimal multipliers give the same linear prediction in direction \(h\) exactly when \(y^\top h\) is constant on \(Y^*(b)\). In particular, the shadow price of coordinate \(i\) is unambiguous exactly when \(y_i\) is constant over \(Y^*(b)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonunique shadow-price vector can still give a unique marginal value in directions on which all optimal multipliers agree.
assumptions_latex: The one-sided direction \(h\) remains within the finite domain of the value function.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \bigl(\forall y^0,y^1\in Y^*(b),\ (y^0-y^1)^\top h=0\bigr)\iff y^\top h\text{ is independent of }y\in Y^*(b).

notation.meaning: dual optimal multiplier set at the reference right-hand side

children.title: Degeneracy–Multiplicity Correspondence
children.top_down_role: Relationship between dual degeneracy and nonuniqueness of multiplier representations.

knowledge_statements.title: Degeneracy–Multiplicity Correspondence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact boundary between redundant dual activity and multiplier nonuniqueness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F_D\) be the dual optimal face and let \(y\in\operatorname{relint}(F_D)\). Set \(K=\{j:A_j^\top y=c_j\}\). Then
\[
\dim F_D=m-\operatorname{rank}(A_K).
\]
Thus optimal multipliers are nonunique exactly when \(\operatorname{rank}(A_K)<m\). By contrast, dual degeneracy at a vertex is the redundancy condition \(|K|>m=\operatorname{rank}(A_K)\). Therefore dual degeneracy and multiplier multiplicity are not equivalent: a unique dual optimum can be degenerate because too many inequalities define one full-rank vertex, while multiplicity requires a rank-deficient affine hull of the optimal face.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Redundant active inequalities cause dual degeneracy; rank deficiency causes multiplier multiplicity. A dual optimum may therefore be degenerate yet unique.
assumptions_latex: The dual optimal face \(F_D\) is nonempty.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(|F_D|>1\iff\operatorname{rank}(A_K)<m\), whereas vertex degeneracy requires \(|K|>m\).

notation.meaning: active set at a relative-interior dual optimum

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Logical Independence of Dual Degeneracy and Multiplier Multiplicity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equality-form LPs witnessing both failures of equivalence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(P_1=\max\{0:x_1+x_2=1,\ x\ge0\}\), the dual is \(\min\{y:y\ge0,\ y\ge0\}\). Its unique optimum \(y=0\) has two active inequalities in dimension one and is degenerate. Conversely, for \(P_2=\max\{-x_3:x_2-x_3=0,\ x_1=1,\ x\ge0\}\), the dual optimal set is \(\{(y_1,0):0\le y_1\le1\}\); both endpoint vertices are determined by exactly two independent active inequalities and are nondegenerate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: One LP has a unique but degenerate dual optimum; another has multiple dual optima whose endpoint vertices are nondegenerate.
assumptions_latex: The dual convention is \(\min\{b^\top y:A^\top y\ge c\}\) for \(\max\{c^\top x:Ax=b,\ x\ge0\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Dual degeneracy}\not\Rightarrow\text{multiplier multiplicity},\qquad \text{multiplier multiplicity}\not\Rightarrow\text{degeneracy of optimal vertices}.

notation.meaning: the two displayed primal linear programs

children.title: Alternative Optimal Solutions
children.top_down_role: Nonunique primal optimizers lying on a nontrivial optimal face.

knowledge_statements.title: Alternative Optimal Solutions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex-geometric characterization of nonunique primal optima.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(P=\{x:Ax=b,\ x\ge0\}\) and suppose the maximum of \(c^\top x\) over \(P\) is attained. Distinct alternative optimal solutions exist exactly when the optimal face
\[
F_P=\{x\in P:c^\top x=z^*\}
\]
has positive dimension. Equivalently, there are an optimal point \(x^*\), a nonzero direction \(d\), and \(\varepsilon>0\) such that \(Ad=0\), \(c^\top d=0\), and \(x^*+td\ge0\) for every \(t\in[0,\varepsilon]\). Every point on that segment is then optimal.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Alternative optima exist exactly when a nonzero feasible direction preserves the objective, equivalently when the primal optimal face has positive dimension.
assumptions_latex: \(P\neq\varnothing\) and the finite optimum \(z^*\) is attained.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(|F_P|>1\iff\dim F_P>0\iff\) a nonzero feasible objective-neutral direction exists.

children.title: Zero Reduced Costs
children.top_down_role: Zero reduced-cost patterns associated with directions along an optimal face.

knowledge_statements.title: Zero Reduced Costs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reduced-cost implications at a primal-dual optimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For the primal-dual pair \(\max\{c^\top x:Ax=b,\ x\ge0\}\) and \(\min\{b^\top y:A^\top y\ge c\}\), define the dual slack, or nonnegative reduced-cost magnitude, by \(s=A^\top y-c\ge0\). At any optimal pair \((x^*,y^*)\), complementary slackness gives
\[
x_j^*s_j^*=0\quad\text{for every }j.
\]
Hence every variable positive in an optimal solution has zero reduced cost. A nonbasic variable with \(s_j^*=0\) is an objective-neutral candidate for entering a basis, but under degeneracy this condition alone need not produce a distinct feasible optimal point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Positive optimal variables must have zero reduced cost. A zero-reduced-cost nonbasic variable signals a possible alternative optimum, but degeneracy can make the associated pivot stationary.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_j^*>0\Rightarrow s_j^*=0\); the converse and alternative-optimum implication need not hold.

children.title: Alternative-Optimum Diagnostics
children.top_down_role: Basis-sensitive interpretation of reduced-cost evidence for optimal multiplicity.

knowledge_statements.title: Alternative-Optimum Diagnostics
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Basis-direction test distinguishing genuine alternatives from degenerate zero-cost pivots.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given an optimal basic feasible solution with basis matrix \(B\), basic vector \(x_B=B^{-1}b\), and a nonbasic index \(j\) having zero reduced cost, form \(d_j=1\), \(d_k=0\) for other nonbasic indices, and \(d_B=-B^{-1}A_j\). Compute
\[
\theta_{\max}=\min_{i:(d_B)_i<0}\frac{(x_B)_i}{-(d_B)_i},
\]
with \(\theta_{\max}=+\infty\) if the index set is empty. If \(\theta_{\max}>0\), output \(x+\theta d\) for any \(0<\theta\le\theta_{\max}\) as a distinct optimum. If \(\theta_{\max}=0\), this pivot direction certifies only a degenerate basis change, not an alternative point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Test each zero-cost entering direction with the ratio test. A positive step yields a distinct optimum; a zero step indicates only a degenerate pivot.
assumptions_latex: \(B\) is an optimal basis for an equality-form primal linear program.
The selected nonbasic index \(j\) has zero reduced cost.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\theta_{\max}>0\) yields a distinct optimal solution along \(d\); \(\theta_{\max}=0\) does not.

notation.meaning: simplex direction for entering variable j

children.title: Degenerate Diagnostic Boundary
children.top_down_role: Limits on inferring distinct optimal solutions from zero reduced costs alone.

knowledge_statements.title: Degenerate Diagnostic Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distinguishes zero-reduced-cost pivots that change the optimizer from degenerate basis changes that do not.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(\max\{c^Tx:Ax=b,\ x\ge 0\}\) at an optimal basic feasible solution with basis \(B\), nonbasic set \(N\), and reduced costs \(\bar c_N=c_N-A_N^TB^{-T}c_B\le0\). For \(j\in N\) with \(\bar c_j=0\), define \(d_j=1\), \(d_{N\setminus\{j\}}=0\), and \(d_B=-B^{-1}A_j\). Let \(\theta^*=\sup\{\theta\ge0:x_B+\theta d_B\ge0\}\). If \(\theta^*>0\), then every sufficiently small \(\theta>0\) gives a distinct optimal solution \(x+\theta d\). If \(\theta^*=0\), the zero reduced cost permits only a degenerate pivot and does not alone certify a distinct optimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A zero reduced cost identifies a distinct alternative optimum only when its simplex direction admits a positive feasible step; a zero step may merely change bases.
assumptions_latex: \(\bar c_N\le0\), so the current basis is optimal.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\theta^*>0\Rightarrow x+\theta d\) is a distinct optimum for \(0<\theta\le\theta^*\); \(\theta^*=0\) is diagnostically inconclusive for solution multiplicity.

notation.meaning: Reduced costs of nonbasic variables under the maximization convention.
Simplex direction generated by entering variable j.
Maximum feasible step along the direction.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Zero Reduced Cost with a Unique Feasible Point
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimal instance showing that a zero-cost nonbasic direction can have zero feasible step and no alternative optimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(\max\{0:x_1+x_2=0,\ x_1,x_2\ge0\}\). Its unique feasible and optimal point is \(x=(0,0)\). With basis \(B=\{1\}\), the nonbasic variable \(x_2\) has zero reduced cost, but its simplex direction is \(d=(-1,1)\), so \(\sup\{\theta\ge0:x+\theta d\ge0\}=0\). Thus the zero reduced cost does not imply a distinct optimal solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A zero-reduced-cost nonbasic variable can be blocked at zero step even when the primal optimizer is unique.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \bar c_2=0\ \text{and}\ \theta^*=0\ \text{while the optimizer is unique}.

maximum feasible step along the direction

knowledge_statements.title: Optimal-Basis Certificate Recovery
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extracts exact primal, dual, and reduced-cost optimality evidence from a reported simplex basis.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\max\{c^Tx:Ax=b,\ x\ge0\}\), input a basis index set \(\mathcal B\) with nonsingular \(B=A_{\mathcal B}\). Compute \(x_{\mathcal B}=B^{-1}b\), \(x_{\mathcal N}=0\), solve \(B^Ty=c_{\mathcal B}\), and form \(s=A^Ty-c\). Return \((x,y,s,\mathcal B)\) only after checking \(Ax=b\), \(x\ge0\), \(s\ge0\), and \(x^Ts=0\). These equalities and inequalities constitute a directly checkable optimal-basis certificate; otherwise report that the supplied basis does not certify optimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Recover the basic primal solution, basis multipliers, and reduced costs, then verify feasibility and complementarity before accepting the basis as optimal.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Ax=b,\ x\ge0,\ A^Ty-c=s\ge0,\ x^Ts=0\Rightarrow c^Tx=b^Ty\) and \(x,y\) are primal-dual optimal.

notation.meaning: Dual slack, equivalently the negative of maximization reduced costs.

knowledge_statements.title: Primal-Dual Solution Certificate Recovery
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Packages paired solver output into feasibility, duality-gap, and complementarity checks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the primal-dual pair \(\max\{c^Tx:Ax=b,\ x\ge0\}\) and \(\min\{b^Ty:A^Ty-s=c,\ s\ge0\}\), a reported triple \((x,y,s)\) is an optimality certificate when \(r_p=Ax-b=0\), \(r_d=A^Ty-s-c=0\), \(x\ge0\), \(s\ge0\), and \(x_is_i=0\) for every \(i\). Equivalently, after feasibility is checked, the gap \(g=b^Ty-c^Tx=x^Ts\) must vanish. For floating-point output, the certificate must retain the residuals, sign violations, gap, and declared verification tolerances rather than asserting exact optimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Paired primal-dual output certifies optimality when both sides are feasible and their gap, equivalently total complementarity, is zero.
assumptions_latex: \((x,y,s)\) is supplied in the original model coordinates.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(r_p=r_d=0,\ x\ge0,\ s\ge0,\ x^Ts=0\Rightarrow x\) and \((y,s)\) are optimal with \(c^Tx=b^Ty\).

children.title: Phase I Farkas Certificate Extraction
children.top_down_role: Infeasibility-witness recovery from auxiliary feasibility models and their terminal bases.

knowledge_statements.title: Phase I Farkas Certificate Extraction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extracts a Farkas witness from a positive-optimum Phase I auxiliary problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: To test \(Ax=b,\ x\ge0\), solve Phase I: \(\min\{\mathbf1^T(u+v):Ax+u-v=b,\ x,u,v\ge0\}\). Its dual is \(\max\{b^Ty:A^Ty\le0,\ -\mathbf1\le y\le\mathbf1\}\). If the terminal Phase I value is positive, recover the dual multiplier \(y\) from the terminal basis and verify \(A^Ty\le0\) and \(b^Ty>0\). Return \(y\), optionally normalized by \(b^Ty=1\), as the infeasibility certificate. Reject the extraction if either inequality fails under the chosen exact or tolerance-aware verifier.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A positive Phase I optimum yields a dual multiplier whose nonpositive column products and positive right-hand-side product certify primal infeasibility.
assumptions_latex: \(u,v\in\mathbb R_+^m\) are artificial variables, making Phase I feasible.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(A^Ty\le0\) and \(b^Ty>0\Rightarrow\{x\ge0:Ax=b\}=\varnothing\).

notation.meaning: Positive and negative artificial residual variables.

children.title: Dual-Simplex Infeasibility Extraction
children.top_down_role: Infeasibility evidence obtained from dual-feasible basis representations and termination states.

knowledge_statements.title: Dual-Simplex Infeasibility Extraction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extracts a Farkas witness from a dual-simplex row having no admissible entering column.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(Ax=b,\ x\ge0\), let \(B\) be the terminal dual-feasible basis and \(\beta=B^{-1}b\). Suppose a row \(i\) satisfies \(\beta_i<0\) and \((B^{-1}A_j)_i\ge0\) for every nonbasic column \(j\); this is the no-entering-column termination condition under the stated tableau convention. Set \(y=-B^{-T}e_i\). Verify against all original columns that \(A^Ty\le0\) and compute \(b^Ty=-\beta_i>0\). Return \(y\), optionally scaled to \(b^Ty=1\); otherwise reject the purported certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At dual-simplex infeasibility termination, the obstructing tableau row produces a Farkas multiplier verifiable against the original matrix and right-hand side.
assumptions_latex: \(B\) is nonsingular and uses the tableau equation \(x_B=B^{-1}b-B^{-1}A_Nx_N\).
\(\beta_i<0\) and the terminal row has no coefficient permitting a feasibility-restoring pivot.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(y=-B^{-T}e_i\), \(A^Ty\le0\), and \(b^Ty>0\) certify infeasibility of \(Ax=b,\ x\ge0\).

notation.meaning: Basic primal values in the terminal basis.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Decodes infeasibility witnesses from one explicitly stated homogeneous primal-dual convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\max\{c^Tx:Ax=b,\ x\ge0\}\), consider a nonzero terminal vector satisfying \(Ax-b\tau=0\), \(A^Ty-s-c\tau=0\), \(c^Tx-b^Ty-\kappa=0\), with \(x,s,\tau,\kappa\ge0\) and \(y\) free. If \(\tau>0\), division by \(\tau\) recovers a primal-dual optimal pair. If \(\tau=0\) and \(\kappa>0\), then \(\kappa=c^Tx-b^Ty\): when \(b^Ty<0\), return \(z=-y\), for which \(A^Tz=-s\le0\) and \(b^Tz>0\), as a primal-infeasibility certificate; when \(c^Tx>0\), return \(x\), for which \(Ax=0\) and \(x\ge0\), as a dual-infeasibility certificate. Verify every returned witness against the original data. The branch \(\tau=\kappa=0\) supplies no strict status certificate under these tests.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under the stated homogeneous equations, a zero-scale positive-certificate outcome yields a verified primal- or dual-infeasibility witness according to which strict pairing is present.
assumptions_latex: The terminal vector satisfies the displayed embedding equations in original, unscaled coordinates.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: b^Ty<0\Rightarrow(A^T(-y)\le0,\ b^T(-y)>0);\qquad c^Tx>0\Rightarrow(Ax=0,\ x\ge0,\ c^Tx>0).
knowledge_statements.title: Fixed-Convention Homogeneous Status Decoding
Homogeneous Self-Dual Certificate Extraction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classifies a homogeneous self-dual terminal vector by verifying its original-space witness components.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\max\{c^Tx:Ax=b,\ x\ge0\}\), input a terminal homogeneous self-dual embedding vector with homogenizing variables \((\tau,\kappa)\). If \(\tau>0\), dehomogenize the primal-dual components by \(\tau\) and verify an optimality certificate. If \(\tau=0\) and \(\kappa>0\), inspect the embedded components: return a primal-infeasibility witness \(y\) only if \(A^Ty\le0\) and \(b^Ty>0\); return an improving primal ray \(d\) only if \(Ad=0\), \(d\ge0\), and \(c^Td>0\). Normalize the returned witness and verify it in original coordinates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dehomogenize an embedding solution when possible; otherwise classify and verify its components as a Farkas witness or improving primal ray.
assumptions_latex: The embedding uses the stated primal maximization convention and identifies \(\tau\) and \(\kappa\).
\(A\), \(b\), and \(c\) denote the unscaled original model data.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A returned \(y\) certifies primal infeasibility; a returned \(d\) certifies primal unboundedness from any primal feasible point.

notation.meaning: Embedding homogenization variable used for dehomogenization.
Embedding status variable separating solution and certificate outcomes.

children.title: Unboundedness Certificate Extraction
children.top_down_role: Recovery of improving rays from simplex and primal-dual solver termination representations.

children.title: Simplex Improving-Ray Extraction
children.top_down_role: Recovery of recession witnesses from simplex unboundedness termination.

knowledge_statements.title: Simplex Improving-Ray Extraction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Recovers an improving recession direction from simplex unboundedness termination.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\max\{c^Tx:Ax=b,\ x\ge0\}\), let \(x\) be a feasible basic solution with basis \(B\). If a nonbasic entering column \(j\) has positive reduced cost \(\bar c_j=c_j-c_B^TB^{-1}A_j>0\) and \(B^{-1}A_j\le0\), the ratio test has no leaving variable. Define \(d_j=1\), \(d_{N\setminus\{j\}}=0\), and \(d_B=-B^{-1}A_j\). Return \(d\) after verifying \(Ad=0\), \(d\ge0\), and \(c^Td=\bar c_j>0\). Then \(x+\theta d\) is feasible for every \(\theta\ge0\) and has unboundedly increasing objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When an improving entering column has no leaving row, its tableau direction is a nonnegative feasible ray with strictly positive objective slope.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Ad=0,\ d\ge0,\ c^Td>0\Rightarrow c^T(x+\theta d)\to+\infty\) as \(\theta\to\infty\).

notation.meaning: Reduced cost of the entering variable.

children.title: Embedded Ray Extraction
children.top_down_role: Recovery of primal or dual ray certificates from homogeneous embedding representations.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Projects zero-scale components from an explicitly stated homogeneous embedding and distinguishes status rays from unboundedness certificates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Use the homogeneous convention \(Ax-b\tau=0\), \(A^Ty-s-c\tau=0\), \(c^Tx-b^Ty-\kappa=0\), with \(x,s,\tau,\kappa\ge0\). At \(\tau=0\), a component \(d=x\) with \(c^Td>0\) satisfies \(Ad=0\), \(d\ge0\); normalize and return it after original-data verification. It certifies primal unboundedness above only when accompanied by a verified primal feasible point. Likewise, if \(b^Ty<0\), the pair \((y,s)\) satisfies \(A^Ty-s=0\), \(s\ge0\) and is a decreasing dual recession direction; it certifies dual unboundedness below only when accompanied by a verified dual feasible point. A zero projected component or zero objective slope is not an unboundedness certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Extract and verify zero-scale primal or dual recession components, but declare unboundedness only when the improving ray is paired with feasibility on the same side.
assumptions_latex: The terminal vector satisfies the displayed embedding convention.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Ad=0,\ d\ge0,\ c^Td>0\text{ plus primal feasibility certifies primal unboundedness; }A^Ty-s=0,\ s\ge0,\ b^Ty<0\text{ plus dual feasibility certifies dual unboundedness}.

notation.meaning: Projected dual-variable and dual-slack recession direction.

knowledge_statements.title: Fixed-Convention Embedded Ray Extraction
Embedded Ray Extraction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Recovers and validates recession certificates encoded by a homogeneous embedding outcome.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a homogeneous embedding terminal vector with \(\tau=0\) and a nonzero candidate ray component, project that component to the original model coordinates and choose its sign and positive normalization according to the embedding convention. For the primal maximization model, accept \(d\) only when \(Ad=0\), \(d\ge0\), and \(c^Td>0\). For a dual improving ray, accept \((q,r)\) only when \(A^Tq-r=0\), \(r\ge0\), and \(b^Tq<0\). Return the accepted normalized ray together with original-space residuals; otherwise report extraction failure.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Project an embedding ray into original coordinates and accept it only after checking the appropriate primal or dual recession and objective conditions.
assumptions_latex: The embedding-to-original coordinate projection and sign convention are available.
The terminal vector has \(\tau=0\) and a nonzero certificate component.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: An accepted \(d\) certifies primal unboundedness from primal feasibility; an accepted \((q,r)\) certifies dual unboundedness from dual feasibility.

children.title: Certificate Recovery Across Model Transformations
children.top_down_role: The mapping of reduced, scaled, or transformed-model certificates back to the original LP representation.

children.title: Certificate Lifting After Presolve
children.top_down_role: Recovery of original-model witnesses from presolved or reduced LP certificates.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local preservation conditions sufficient for sound reverse lifting through a presolve sequence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M_0\xrightarrow{T_1}M_1\xrightarrow{T_2}\cdots\xrightarrow{T_k}M_k\) be presolve transformations. For a fixed certificate type, let \(P_i(z)\) be its validity predicate on \(M_i\). If every stored lift \(L_i\) satisfies \[P_i(z)\Longrightarrow P_{i-1}(L_i z),\] then \[P_k(z_k)\Longrightarrow P_0((L_1\circ L_2\circ\cdots\circ L_k)z_k).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If every reverse presolve step preserves certificate validity, their reverse composition lifts a valid reduced certificate to a valid original certificate.
assumptions_latex: Each presolve step has a certificate-type-specific lift satisfying the displayed preservation implication.
The lifts are applied in reverse transformation order.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Local certificate preservation implies soundness of the complete postsolve lift.

notation.meaning: Model after the first \(i\) presolve transformations.
Lift from certificates of \(M_i\) to certificates of \(M_{i-1}\).

knowledge_statements.title: Compositional Soundness of Certificate Lifting
Certificate Lifting After Presolve
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Replays reversible presolve transformations to lift a reduced-model certificate into the original LP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a reduced-model certificate \(z_k\) and an ordered presolve log \((T_1,\ldots,T_k)\), where each entry stores an inverse certificate map \(L_i\) for its transformation. Initialize \(z=z_k\). For \(i=k,k-1,\ldots,1\), set \(z\leftarrow L_i(z)\), restoring eliminated primal variables, dual multipliers, slacks, rays, or objective offsets as required by \(T_i\). After replay, verify the resulting \(z_0\) directly against the original \((A,b,c)\) using the certificate-type predicates. Return \(z_0\) only if every original-space residual, sign condition, and strict certificate inequality passes.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Lift a presolved certificate by reversing every recorded transformation, then validate the reconstructed witness directly against the original LP.
assumptions_latex: Every presolve transformation records a certificate-aware inverse map \(L_i\).
The reduced certificate type is known and valid for the reduced model.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Successful reverse replay and original-space verification produce a certificate for the unpresolved LP.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Reverse replay followed by original-space verification is a reasonable generic framework, but no source supports the asserted certificate-aware inverse maps, and their existence and form depend on each presolve transformation.

children.title: Certificate Recovery Interface
children.top_down_role: Restoration of certificates after numerical scaling, substitutions, and representation changes.

children.title: Certificate Unscaling
children.top_down_role: Restoration of certificate magnitudes after row, column, or objective scaling.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extends positive row and column unscaling to a positive scalar objective scaling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\max\{c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax\le b\}\), let \(R,D\) be positive diagonal and \(\alpha>0\), with \(\widehat A=RAD\), \(\widehat b=Rb\), and \(\widehat c=\alpha Dc\). If \(\widehat A^{\mathsf T}\widehat y-\widehat c=\widehat s\), then original-coordinate quantities are \[x=D\widehat x,\qquad y=\alpha^{-1}R\widehat y,\qquad s=\alpha^{-1}D^{-1}\widehat s.\] The scaled primal and dual objective values are \(\alpha\) times their corresponding original values.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A positive objective scaling divides reconstructed dual multipliers and dual slacks by the objective factor while leaving the primal coordinate map unchanged.
assumptions_latex: \(R\) and \(D\) are positive diagonal and nonsingular.
The displayed scaled-data convention is used.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The stated maps restore original stationarity, signs, and primal–dual objective scale.

notation.meaning: Positive scalar multiplying the scaled objective.

knowledge_statements.title: Objective-Scaling Rule for Primal–Dual Certificates
Certificate Unscaling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Maps primal, dual, slack, and ray certificates through positive row and column scalings.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let positive diagonal matrices \(R\) and \(D\) define scaled data \(\widehat A=RAD\), \(\widehat b=Rb\), and \(\widehat c=Dc\) for the primal maximization form. From a scaled primal-dual certificate \((\widehat x,\widehat y,\widehat s)\), reconstruct \(x=D\widehat x\), \(y=R\widehat y\), and \(s=D^{-1}\widehat s\). Unscale primal rays by \(d=D\widehat d\) and Farkas multipliers by \(y_F=R\widehat y_F\). Return the reconstructed object only after verifying its defining equalities, signs, complementarity, and any strict objective inequality against \((A,b,c)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Undo positive row and column scaling with the corresponding primal, dual, slack, and ray maps, then recheck the original model.
assumptions_latex: \(R\) and \(D\) are positive diagonal and nonsingular.
The scaled model uses \(\widehat A=RAD\), \(\widehat b=Rb\), and \(\widehat c=Dc\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Valid scaled certificates map to valid original-space certificates under the displayed unscaling formulas.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The displayed unscaling formulas are internally consistent with the declared scaled model, and the algorithm fits the leaf, but the record supplies no citation with an inspectable locator.

children.title: Original-Space Reconstruction
children.top_down_role: Recovery of certificate objects in the variables and constraints of the original model.

knowledge_statements.title: Original-Space Reconstruction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reconstructs eliminated coordinates and multipliers before validating a certificate on the original model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose model reduction represents original primal variables by \(x=Pz+q\) and records compatible inverse rules for eliminated constraints, dual multipliers, slacks, and rays. Given a reduced certificate, first reconstruct \(x\); then apply the stored adjoint and substitution rules in reverse order to recover original dual variables and slacks, using the homogeneous map \(d=P\delta\) for rays. Restore fixed variables and objective offsets explicitly. Finally evaluate the applicable original-space predicate: primal-dual feasibility and zero gap, Farkas inequalities, or recession and strict improvement conditions. Output the reconstructed witness only when that predicate holds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Recover eliminated variables and multipliers using stored inverse transformations, then verify the completed witness solely with the original LP data.
assumptions_latex: The reduction stores the affine primal map and inverse rules for every eliminated row and column.
Reduced and original certificate types are identified consistently.
The original model data remain available for final verification.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Passing the original-space certificate predicate makes the reconstructed object independent of the reduced representation.

notation.meaning: Linear and offset parts of the primal reconstruction map.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The primal affine reconstruction and homogeneous ray map are plausible, but recovery of dual multipliers and slacks is transformation-specific and is described only generically. No source supports the required inverse and adjoint rules.

children.title: Transformation Traceability
children.top_down_role: Provenance needed to map transformed certificate components back to source-model objects.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Specifies the generic replay contract while leaving transformation-specific reconstruction to sibling leaves.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a terminal certificate \(w_k\) of class \(\mathcal C\), process the ordered transformation log in reverse and set \(w_{i-1}=L_i^{\mathcal C}(w_i)\). Reject if a required lift is absent, its recorded parameters or identifiers are insufficient to determine one result, or an intermediate precondition fails. After the final lift, accept only if \(V_0^{\mathcal C}(w_0)\) holds on the original model data.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Replay certificate lifts in reverse order and accept the result only after direct original-model verification.
assumptions_latex: The log is ordered and identifies the certificate class.
Each invoked lift has its required recorded parameters.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: w_0=(L_1^{\mathcal C}\circ\cdots\circ L_k^{\mathcal C})w_k\text{ is returned only if }V_0^{\mathcal C}(w_0).
knowledge_statements.title: Reverse Trace Replay

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines traceability abstractly without prescribing solver-specific metadata fields.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M_0,\ldots,M_k\) be successive LP representations and let \(V_i^{\mathcal C}(w)\) mean that \(w\) is a valid certificate of class \(\mathcal C\) for \(M_i\). The transformation log is traceable for \(\mathcal C\) if it determines, for every step, a certificate lift \(L_i^{\mathcal C}\) such that \(V_i^{\mathcal C}(w)\Rightarrow V_{i-1}^{\mathcal C}(L_i^{\mathcal C}w)\), including all recorded indices and parameters needed to evaluate the map deterministically. The complete lift is \(L_1^{\mathcal C}\circ\cdots\circ L_k^{\mathcal C}\). Traceability is certificate-class-specific: a sequence may be traceable for primal points but not for dual multipliers or rays.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A transformation sequence is traceable for a certificate class exactly when its log determines validity-preserving lifts through every step back to the original model.
assumptions_latex: A verification predicate \(V_i^{\mathcal C}\) is fixed for each supported certificate class.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: V_k^{\mathcal C}(w)\Rightarrow V_0^{\mathcal C}\!\left((L_1^{\mathcal C}\circ\cdots\circ L_k^{\mathcal C})w\right).

notation.meaning: Certificate-verification predicate for class C on representation i.
Recorded backward certificate lift for one transformation.

knowledge_statements.title: Certificate-Class Traceability
Transformation Traceability
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Specifies the transformation metadata required for reproducible certificate recovery.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A model-transformation sequence is certificate-traceable when every step \(T_i:M_{i-1}\to M_i\) records: its type and exact parameters; forward maps for feasible points and rays; inverse or lifting maps for each supported certificate class; adjoint maps for dual multipliers and slacks; changes to bounds, signs, senses, and objective offsets; and the identifiers of affected rows and columns. The ordered log must permit deterministic reverse composition \(L_1\circ\cdots\circ L_k\) and retain enough original data to check the lifted object directly on \(M_0\). A sequence lacking any required inverse rule is not traceable for that certificate class.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Certificate recovery is traceable only when every model transformation records ordered, certificate-aware forward, inverse, adjoint, indexing, and objective metadata.
assumptions_latex: Each supported certificate class has a specified verification predicate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Traceability holds exactly for certificate classes whose witnesses can be deterministically lifted and verified on \(M_0\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition is coherent and fits the traceability leaf, but its claimed necessary metadata and exact characterization are interface-dependent and have no cited authoritative source or locator.

children.title: Reconstruction Failure Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Information-loss and inconsistency boundaries affecting certificate recovery.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Nonuniqueness Does Not Preclude Valid-Witness Recovery
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distinguishes recovery of a particular original certificate from recovery of some valid original certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\subseteq Z\) be an admissible certificate set and \(T:C\to\widetilde Z\). If \(T\) is noninjective, no map \(R\) can satisfy \(R(Tz)=z\) for every \(z\in C\). Nevertheless, noninjectivity alone does not preclude validity recovery: if \(C=\{z_1,z_2\}\), \(z_1\ne z_2\), and \(Tz_1=Tz_2=w\), then \(R(w)=z_1\) returns an admissible certificate. Thus loss of certificate identity is weaker than loss of every valid lift.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A many-to-one transformation prevents recovery of the particular original certificate but may still permit recovery of some valid original certificate.
assumptions_latex: Every element of \(C\) is a valid original-space certificate.
The recovery goal distinguishes identity recovery from validity recovery.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Noninjectivity obstructs identity recovery but does not by itself obstruct existence of a valid-witness section.
knowledge_statements.title: Nonuniqueness Does Not Preclude Valid-Witness Recovery
Reconstruction Failure Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Information-loss boundary for recovering original-space LP certificates after model transformations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let an LP transformation map original certificates by a linear map \(T:Z\to\widetilde Z\). Exact reconstruction from the transformed certificate alone requires a recovery map \(R\) satisfying \(R(Tz)=z\) on the admissible certificate set \(C\subseteq Z\). If distinct certificates \(z_1,z_2\in C\) satisfy \(Tz_1=Tz_2\), then no such recovery map exists. Consequently, eliminations, aggregations, scaling operations with discarded factors, or deleted redundant rows can prevent recovery of original multipliers or rays unless the transformation trace stores enough auxiliary data to distinguish every admissible preimage.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Original certificates cannot be reconstructed when a transformation identifies distinct admissible certificates, unless retained trace data distinguishes their preimages.
assumptions_latex: \(T:Z\to\widetilde Z\) is the certificate map induced by the model transformation.
\(C\subseteq Z\) is the set of admissible original-space certificates.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists z_1\ne z_2\text{ in }C:\ Tz_1=Tz_2\ \Longrightarrow\ \nexists R\text{ with }R\circ T=I_C.\)

notation.meaning: Map from original-space to transformed-space certificates.

children.title: Resource Shadow Prices
children.top_down_role: Multiplier interpretations attached to scarce resource balances.

knowledge_statements.title: Resource Shadow Prices
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dual prices attached to resource-consumption constraints in a maximization LP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the primal LP \(v(b)=\max\{c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax\le b,\ x\ge0\}\) and its dual \(\min\{b^{\mathsf T}y:A^{\mathsf T}y\ge c,\ y\ge0\}\), an optimal dual component \(y_i^*\) is a resource shadow price for resource row \(i\). It is a global supergradient component of the concave value function: for every right-hand side \(b'\) for which the primal value is finite, \(v(b')\le v(b)+(y^*)^{\mathsf T}(b'-b)\). Where \(v\) is differentiable at \(b\), the local marginal value of resource \(i\) equals \(y_i^*=\partial v(b)/\partial b_i\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A resource shadow price is an optimal dual multiplier, giving a supergradient—and, when differentiable, the marginal value—of available resource.
assumptions_latex: Strong duality holds and \(y^*\) is dual optimal.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(v(b')\le v(b)+(y^*)^{\mathsf T}(b'-b)\), and differentiability implies \(y_i^*=\partial v(b)/\partial b_i\).

notation.meaning: Optimal primal value at resource vector b.

children.title: Capacity Shadow Prices
children.top_down_role: Multiplier interpretations attached to upper-capacity restrictions.

knowledge_statements.title: Capacity Shadow Prices
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Marginal values of upper-bound capacities under the maximization convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(v(u)=\max\{c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax\le u,\ x\ge0\}\). A capacity shadow-price vector at \(u\) is any optimal solution \(y^*\) of \(\min\{u^{\mathsf T}y:A^{\mathsf T}y\ge c,\ y\ge0\}\). Thus \(y_i^*\ge0\), and complementary slackness gives \(y_i^*(u_i-a_i^{\mathsf T}x^*)=0\) for every primal optimum \(x^*\). Moreover, if the same vector \(y^*\) remains dual optimal for \(u+t e_i\) for every \(t\in[0,\varepsilon]\), then \(v(u+t e_i)-v(u)=t y_i^*\) throughout that interval.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A capacity shadow price is a nonnegative dual multiplier on an upper-capacity constraint. It gives the exact value of added capacity over an interval when the selected dual solution remains optimal throughout that interval.
assumptions_latex: The primal and dual optima \(x^*\) and \(y^*\) exist.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(y_i^*\ge0\) and \(y_i^*(u_i-a_i^{\mathsf T}x^*)=0\); if \(y^*\) remains dual optimal on \(u+t e_i\) for \(t\in[0,\varepsilon]\), then \(v(u+t e_i)-v(u)=t y_i^*\).

notation.meaning: Row i of the constraint matrix.

children.title: Resource–Capacity Price Correspondence
children.top_down_role: Relationship between resource-balance values and capacity-bound values.

knowledge_statements.title: Resource–Capacity Price Correspondence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Correspondence between physical resource values and dual capacity multipliers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: In \(v(b)=\max\{c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax\le b,\ x\ge0\}\), suppose primal and dual optima exist. Strong duality yields \(c^{\mathsf T}x^*=b^{\mathsf T}y^*\), while complementary slackness yields \(y_i^*(b_i-a_i^{\mathsf T}x^*)=0\). Hence the price assigned to resource \(i\) is exactly the dual price of its capacity row. Unused capacity forces zero price, whereas a positive price forces the corresponding capacity to be fully used. The converse need not hold: a binding capacity may have zero price under degeneracy or local redundancy.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Resource prices equal capacity-row dual multipliers; positive prices imply full use, while binding capacity alone need not imply a positive price.
assumptions_latex: \(x^*\) and \(y^*\) are primal and dual optimal.
The primal uses the maximization form \(Ax\le b\), \(x\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(c^{\mathsf T}x^*=b^{\mathsf T}y^*\quad\text{and}\quad y_i^*(b_i-a_i^{\mathsf T}x^*)=0.\)

notation.meaning: Common resource and capacity shadow price.

children.title: Scarcity-Price Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Regimes limiting marginal scarcity interpretations of dual multipliers.

knowledge_statements.title: Scarcity-Price Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Limits of inferring economic scarcity from LP dual multipliers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(v(b)=\max\{c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax\le b,\ x\ge0\}\), any dual optimum \(y^*\) satisfies \(y_i^*>0\Rightarrow a_i^{\mathsf T}x^*=b_i\) by complementary slackness. Neither reverse implication nor a globally valid marginal interpretation follows: a binding row may have \(y_i^*=0\), distinct dual optima may assign different prices, and a selected price predicts value changes only while the associated dual solution remains optimal. Thus positivity certifies scarcity relative to the modeled LP, but zero price does not by itself certify physical abundance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Positive price implies a binding modeled capacity, but binding need not imply positive price, and marginal interpretations are local and possibly nonunique.
assumptions_latex: The primal and dual have optimal solutions.
\(y^*\) is an optimal multiplier for \(Ax\le b\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(y_i^*>0\Rightarrow a_i^{\mathsf T}x^*=b_i\), but \(a_i^{\mathsf T}x^*=b_i\not\Rightarrow y_i^*>0\).

notation.meaning: Selected optimal shadow price for row i.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Binding Capacity with Zero Shadow Price
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Duplicate capacity rows give a sharp counterexample to inferring a positive scarcity price from bindingness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(v(b)=\max\{x:x\le b_1,\ x\le b_2,\ x\ge0\}\) at \(b=(1,1)\), with dual \(\min\{y_1+y_2:y_1+y_2\ge1,\ y\ge0\}\). The primal optimum is \(x^*=1\), so both capacity rows bind, while \(y^*=(1,0)\) is dual optimal. Thus the second capacity is binding but has zero price in a valid optimal price system.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Duplicate binding capacities can admit an optimal price system assigning zero price to one binding row.
assumptions_latex: The primal and dual use the stated maximization and nonnegative-multiplier conventions.

notation.meaning: Dual price of capacity row i.

children.title: Requirement Shadow Prices

knowledge_statements.title: Requirement Shadow Prices
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dual prices attached to minimum-requirement constraints in a cost-minimization LP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(w(d)=\min\{c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax\ge d,\ x\ge0\}\) and its dual \(\max\{d^{\mathsf T}p:A^{\mathsf T}p\le c,\ p\ge0\}\), an optimal component \(p_i^*\) is a requirement shadow price. For every \(d'\) with finite primal value, dual feasibility gives \(w(d')\ge w(d)+(p^*)^{\mathsf T}(d'-d)\), so \(p^*\) is a subgradient of the convex value function. Where \(w\) is differentiable, \(p_i^*=\partial w(d)/\partial d_i\), the local marginal cost of tightening requirement \(i\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A requirement shadow price is an optimal dual multiplier measuring the local cost of increasing a minimum requirement.
assumptions_latex: Strong duality holds and \(p^*\) is dual optimal.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(w(d')\ge w(d)+(p^*)^{\mathsf T}(d'-d)\), and differentiability implies \(p_i^*=\partial w(d)/\partial d_i\).

notation.meaning: Minimum cost at requirement vector d.

knowledge_statements.title: Demand Shadow Prices
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Marginal fulfillment costs for demand constraints in a minimization LP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(w(d)=\min\{c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax\ge d,\ x\ge0\}\). A demand shadow-price vector is any dual optimum \(p^*\in\arg\max\{d^{\mathsf T}p:A^{\mathsf T}p\le c,\ p\ge0\}\). Its components satisfy \(p_i^*\ge0\), and complementary slackness gives \(p_i^*(a_i^{\mathsf T}x^*-d_i)=0\). If the same vector \(p^*\) remains dual optimal for \(d+t e_i\) for every \(t\in[0,\varepsilon]\), then \(w(d+t e_i)-w(d)=t p_i^*\) throughout that interval.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A demand shadow price is a nonnegative dual multiplier. It gives the exact added fulfillment cost over an interval when the selected dual solution remains optimal throughout that interval.
assumptions_latex: Primal and dual optima \(x^*\) and \(p^*\) exist.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p_i^*\ge0\) and \(p_i^*(a_i^{\mathsf T}x^*-d_i)=0\); if \(p^*\) remains dual optimal on \(d+t e_i\) for \(t\in[0,\varepsilon]\), then \(w(d+t e_i)-w(d)=t p_i^*\).

notation.meaning: Row i of the constraint matrix.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Global lower supporting inequality supplied by an optimal demand-price vector.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(w(d)=\min\{c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax\ge d,\ x\ge0\}\), let \(p^*\) be dual optimal at \(d\). For every \(d'\) at which the primal value is finite, dual feasibility gives \[w(d')\ge (d')^{\mathsf T}p^*=w(d)+(p^*)^{\mathsf T}(d'-d).\] Thus \(p^*\) is a subgradient of the convex demand-value function at \(d\). If \(w\) is locally finite at \(d\) and the optimal price vector is unique, then \(w\) is differentiable there and \(\nabla w(d)=p^*\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An optimal demand price globally supports the demand-cost value function from below. Under local finiteness, a unique optimal price is its gradient.
assumptions_latex: Primal and dual optima exist at \(d\), and strong duality holds.
For differentiability, \(w\) is finite on a neighborhood of \(d\) and the optimal dual vector is unique.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(w(d')\ge w(d)+(p^*)^{\mathsf T}(d'-d)\); under local finiteness and uniqueness, \(\nabla w(d)=p^*\).

knowledge_statements.title: Requirement–Demand Price Correspondence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Correspondence between demand marginal costs and minimum-requirement dual multipliers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: In \(w(d)=\min\{c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax\ge d,\ x\ge0\}\), suppose primal and dual optima exist. Strong duality gives \(c^{\mathsf T}x^*=d^{\mathsf T}p^*\), and complementary slackness gives \(p_i^*(a_i^{\mathsf T}x^*-d_i)=0\). Therefore the economic price of demand \(i\) is exactly the dual multiplier of its minimum-requirement row. A positive price forces exact fulfillment of that requirement; excess fulfillment forces zero price. Exact fulfillment alone need not imply a positive price because degeneracy or redundant requirements can produce zero multipliers.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Demand prices equal requirement-row dual multipliers; positive price forces exact fulfillment, but exact fulfillment need not force positive price.
assumptions_latex: \(x^*\) and \(p^*\) are primal and dual optimal.
The primal uses the minimization form \(Ax\ge d\), \(x\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(c^{\mathsf T}x^*=d^{\mathsf T}p^*\quad\text{and}\quad p_i^*(a_i^{\mathsf T}x^*-d_i)=0.\)

children.title: Price-Orientation Conventions
children.top_down_role: Sign and objective-orientation conventions governing requirement or demand price readings.

knowledge_statements.title: Price-Orientation Conventions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sign conversion between raw dual multipliers and nonnegative economic prices.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Economic prices depend on the orientation used to write a constraint. For a maximization LP, writing a capacity as \(a_i^{\mathsf T}x\le b_i\) gives a nonnegative price \(y_i\ge0\); rewriting it as \(-a_i^{\mathsf T}x\ge-b_i\) gives the raw multiplier \(-y_i\le0\). For a minimization LP, writing a requirement as \(a_i^{\mathsf T}x\ge d_i\) gives a nonnegative price \(p_i\ge0\); rewriting it with the opposite orientation gives \(-p_i\le0\). Equality-row multipliers are unrestricted, and reversing the equality reverses their signs without changing the economic valuation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reversing a constraint reverses its raw multiplier; economic prices require a declared orientation, while equality multipliers are sign-unrestricted.
assumptions_latex: Each reversed row represents the same feasible constraint.
The dual objective and multiplier signs are transformed consistently.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((a_i^{\mathsf T}x\le b_i,\ y_i)\equiv(-a_i^{\mathsf T}x\ge-b_i,\ -y_i)\), and analogously for requirement rows.

notation.meaning: Capacity price under the less-than-or-equal orientation.
Requirement price under the greater-than-or-equal orientation.

children.top_down_role: Interpretive limitations caused by multiple dual optima and degeneracy.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonunique Shadow Prices
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Interpretive limitation arising from multiple optimal dual solutions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Y^*(b)=\arg\min\{b^{\mathsf T}y:A^{\mathsf T}y\ge c,\ y\ge0\}\) for \(v(b)=\max\{c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax\le b,\ x\ge0\}\). If \(Y^*(b)\) contains distinct vectors, the LP determines a set of valid shadow-price vectors rather than a unique vector. Every \(y\in Y^*(b)\) is a supergradient of \(v\) at \(b\), and the linear predictions \(y^{\mathsf T}h\) may differ with the selected optimum. If \(v(b+t h)\) is finite for all sufficiently small \(t>0\), then the right directional derivative satisfies \(v'(b;h)=\min_{y\in Y^*(b)}y^{\mathsf T}h\). Thus a multiplier-based price prediction is selection-independent exactly when \(y^{\mathsf T}h\) is constant over \(Y^*(b)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Multiple dual optima produce multiple valid price vectors. Their linear predictions can disagree, although the right directional derivative is the minimum directional pairing among the optimal multipliers when nearby values are finite.
assumptions_latex: The primal has a finite attained optimum.
For the directional-derivative formula, \(v(b+t h)\) is finite for every sufficiently small \(t>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(v'(b;h)=\min_{y\in Y^*(b)}y^{\mathsf T}h\), while the multiplier-based prediction is selection-independent if and only if \(y^{\mathsf T}h\) is constant over \(Y^*(b)\).

notation.meaning: Set of optimal dual price vectors.
Right directional derivative of the value function.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonbasic-Activity Valuations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reduced costs as marginal net values of inactive primal activities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\max\{c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax\le b,\ x\ge0\}\), let \(y^*\) be dual optimal and define the reduced cost \(\bar c_j=c_j-a_j^{\mathsf T}y^*\). Dual feasibility gives \(\bar c_j\le0\), and complementary slackness gives \(x_j^*\bar c_j=0\). For a nonbasic activity with \(x_j^*=0\), \(\bar c_j\) is its unit objective return after charging the resources it consumes at prices \(y^*\). A negative value is the first-order objective loss from activating that column while the current prices and basis remain valid; zero indicates no such local penalty.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The reduced cost of an inactive activity is its return net of priced resource use; negativity indicates local loss and zero indicates no local penalty.
assumptions_latex: The primal and dual optima exist.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\bar c_j=c_j-a_j^{\mathsf T}y^*\le0\quad\text{and}\quad x_j^*\bar c_j=0.\)

notation.meaning: Reduced cost of activity j under the maximization convention.

children.title: Column-Generation Pricing Interface
children.top_down_role: Reduced costs as the dual interface for identifying improving columns.

knowledge_statements.title: Column-Generation Pricing Interface
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dual reduced-cost oracle for detecting improving columns in a restricted master LP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider the full master LP \(\max\{\sum_{j\in\mathcal J}c_jx_j:\sum_{j\in\mathcal J}a_jx_j\le b,\ x_j\ge0\}\) and a restricted master using \(\mathcal J_R\subseteq\mathcal J\). Solve the restricted master to primal-dual optimality and obtain \(y^*\ge0\). The pricing oracle evaluates \(\rho^*=\sup_{j\in\mathcal J\setminus\mathcal J_R}(c_j-a_j^{\mathsf T}y^*)\). If \(\rho^*>0\), the oracle returns an omitted index \(j\) with \(c_j-a_j^{\mathsf T}y^*>0\); add that column and reoptimize. If \(\rho^*\le0\), then \(a_j^{\mathsf T}y^*\ge c_j\) for every omitted column, so \(y^*\) is feasible for the full dual. The restricted primal solution, extended by zeros on omitted columns, and \(y^*\) then certify full-master optimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Solve the restricted master and price every omitted column by reduced cost. Add any column with positive reduced cost; if none exists, the restricted solution and dual vector certify optimality for the full master.
assumptions_latex: The restricted master has been solved to primal-dual optimality.
The pricing oracle evaluates all omitted columns exactly and returns a positive-reduced-cost column whenever \(\rho^*>0\).
The displayed sums and optimization problems are well-defined, and the restricted optimum is finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\rho^*>0\) yields an improving omitted column, whereas \(\rho^*\le0\) makes \(y^*\) full-dual feasible and certifies full-master optimality.

notation.meaning: Optimal dual vector for the restricted master.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Limits of interpreting a reduced-cost tolerance as a full-master objective-gap certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: In the maximization-master convention, a pricing result \(\sup_{j\notin\mathcal J_R}(c_j-a_j^{\mathsf T}y^*)\le\varepsilon\) with \(\varepsilon>0\) does not by itself certify an absolute objective gap of at most \(\varepsilon\). For any \(M>0\), the one-column full master \(\max\{\delta x:x\le M,\ x\ge0\}\), with \(0<\delta\le\varepsilon\), has omitted-column reduced cost \(\delta\) at the empty restricted master but full-master gap \(\delta M\). A quantitative gap bound therefore requires an additional activity bound or another problem-specific error certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A reduced-cost tolerance alone is not an objective-gap tolerance: small positive reduced costs can produce a large improvement when substantial activity is possible.
assumptions_latex: Pricing may terminate while positive reduced costs no larger than \(\varepsilon\) remain.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\rho^*\le\varepsilon\not\Rightarrow z^*_{\mathrm{full}}-z^*_{R}\le\varepsilon\) without an additional structural bound.

notation.meaning: activity upper bound in the counterexample family

children.title: Binding-Structure Explanations
children.top_down_role: Interpretation of optimal multipliers and complementarity as explanations of active model structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Binding-Structure Explanations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional primal-dual LP certificate interpreting positive multipliers through complementary slackness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider the primal problem \(\min\{c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax\ge b,\ x\ge0\}\) and its dual \(\max\{b^{\mathsf T}y:A^{\mathsf T}y\le c,\ y\ge0\}\). For a primal-dual feasible pair \((x^*,y^*)\), define \(s^*=Ax^*-b\) and \(r^*=c-A^{\mathsf T}y^*\). The duality gap decomposes as \[c^{\mathsf T}x^*-b^{\mathsf T}y^*=(x^*)^{\mathsf T}r^*+(y^*)^{\mathsf T}s^*.\] Hence zero gap certifies optimality and is equivalent to \(x_j^*r_j^*=0\) and \(y_i^*s_i^*=0\) for every \(j\) and \(i\). Consequently, \(y_i^*>0\) certifies that primal constraint \(i\) binds, while \(x_j^*>0\) certifies that dual constraint \(j\) binds; the reverse implications need not hold.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A zero-gap feasible primal-dual pair certifies optimality. Positive dual multipliers identify binding primal constraints, and positive primal variables identify tight dual constraints; binding alone need not imply positivity.
assumptions_latex: \((x^*,y^*)\) is feasible for the displayed primal-dual pair.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Zero duality gap certifies optimality, with \(y_i^*>0\Rightarrow (Ax^*-b)_i=0\) and \(x_j^*>0\Rightarrow (c-A^{\mathsf T}y^*)_j=0\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Binding conclusions invariant across the primal and dual optimal faces.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X^*\) and \(Y^*\) be the nonempty optimal sets for the primal-dual pair in the seed. Every \(x\in X^*\) and \(y\in Y^*\) satisfy \(y_i(Ax-b)_i=0\). Consequently, \(y_i>0\) at some dual optimum if and only if constraint \(i\) binds at every primal optimum; equivalently, the constraint is slack at some primal optimum if and only if \(y_i=0\) at every dual optimum. The reverse implication for one selected optimal pair remains invalid: binding at that selected primal optimum need not make its paired multiplier positive.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A multiplier positive at some dual optimum identifies a constraint binding throughout the primal optimal face. Conversely, persistent binding guarantees positivity at some dual optimum, although a selected optimal pair may still assign zero multiplier to a binding constraint.
assumptions_latex: The finite-dimensional LP strict-complementarity theorem applies.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists y\in Y^*:y_i>0\iff\forall x\in X^*:(Ax-b)_i=0\), and \(\exists x\in X^*:(Ax-b)_i>0\iff\forall y\in Y^*:y_i=0\).
knowledge_statements.title: Optimal-Face-Wide Binding Alternatives

children.title: Infeasibility-Conflict Explanations
children.top_down_role: Interpretation of Farkas multipliers as explanations of inconsistent constraint collections.

knowledge_statements.title: Infeasibility-Conflict Explanations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Farkas certificate for an infeasible finite system of linear inequalities with unrestricted variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) and \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), the system \(Ax\le b\), with \(x\in\mathbb R^n\), is infeasible if and only if there exists \(y\in\mathbb R^m\) satisfying \[y\ge0,\qquad A^{\mathsf T}y=0,\qquad b^{\mathsf T}y<0.\] Such a vector is directly checkable and certifies infeasibility because every feasible \(x\) would imply \(0=y^{\mathsf T}Ax\le y^{\mathsf T}b<0\). Moreover, the index set \(I=\{i:y_i>0\}\) identifies an infeasible subsystem: the constraints indexed by \(I\) alone yield the same contradictory nonnegative aggregation. By positive rescaling, the certificate may be normalized so that \(b^{\mathsf T}y=-1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonnegative Farkas multiplier whose weighted left sides cancel and weighted bounds are negative certifies infeasibility. Its positive support identifies a conflicting subset of constraints.
assumptions_latex: The variable \(x\) ranges over all of \(\mathbb R^n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The system \(Ax\le b\) is infeasible exactly when a multiplier \(y\ge0\) satisfies \(A^{\mathsf T}y=0\) and \(b^{\mathsf T}y<0\); its positive support is an infeasible subsystem.

notation.meaning: indices of constraints receiving positive multiplier weight

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distinguishes an arbitrary Farkas-supported conflict from an irreducible infeasible subsystem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(Ax\le b\) with unrestricted \(x\), the positive support \(I(y)=\{i:y_i>0\}\) of any Farkas certificate \(y\ge0\), \(A^{\mathsf T}y=0\), \(b^{\mathsf T}y<0\), indexes an infeasible subsystem but need not be inclusion-minimal. If \(I(y)\) is inclusion-minimal among supports of Farkas certificates, then the subsystem indexed by \(I(y)\) is irreducibly infeasible. Conversely, every inclusion-minimal infeasible subsystem admits a Farkas certificate whose positive support is exactly its index set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Farkas certificate identifies a conflict but not necessarily an irreducible one. Inclusion-minimal certificate supports coincide with inclusion-minimal infeasible subsystems.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), and \(x\in\mathbb R^n\) is unrestricted.
Farkas' alternative applies to each selected subsystem.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(I(y)\) is infeasible, and its inclusion-minimal certificate supports are exactly the inclusion-minimal infeasible subsystems.

notation.meaning: positive support of the Farkas multiplier

knowledge_statements.title: Certificate Support Versus Irreducible Conflict
